title: 5 Signs That Your Laptop Needs Servicing
seoTitle: 5 Signs That Your Laptop Needs Servicing
metaDescription: Learn five common signs that your laptop needs professional servicing, from overheating and slow performance to battery and hardware problems.
excerpt: Learn five common signs that your laptop needs professional servicing, from overheating and slow performance to battery and hardware problems.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: A laptop is an essential piece of equipment for the modern world. As they can be used frequently small issues can occur. You may notice that it now takes several minutes to boot into the laptop, the fan is louder than usual, the keyboard feels hot or the battery doesn’t last long enough to complete a usual working session.

Regular maintenance helps to identify any wear and tear, remove any dust, check the software and ensure key components are running safely. Below are 5 signs that you should consider having a professional look at your laptop:

content.heading: 1. Overheating / Loud Fan
paragraphs: Laptops will run warm when completing a high demand task, but if it is overheating then it could be a sign something is wrong. If the keyboard or bottom is getting too hot to use during normal tasks, or the fan is running loudly whilst using just a browser or document, it could be that your laptop is struggling to cool.

This can happen due to dust build up inside the vents, fan and heatsink blocking airflow. A worn fan, dried thermal paste, blocked vents and/or high demand processes running in the background. This can cause your laptop to slow down to protect the components. This is called thermal throttling, you may notice a slowdown, unexpected shutdowns or slow performance when using video calling, gaming or performing a high demand task.

Ensure your laptop is placed on a firm flat surface, free from covering the vents. Close down any applications using unnecessary processing power. Ensure you are not pushing anything into the vents and only open the laptop if you have the right tools and knowledge. If you are still experiencing overheating issues then a technician can investigate the cooling components, safely remove any dust and check your fan and thermal paste. This is especially important if your laptop is shutting down unexpectedly or running very hot.

content.heading: 2. Slower Performance
paragraphs: Your laptop can run slower due to a variety of reasons. Too many startup programs, low storage space, outdated software, malware, low memory or a failing storage drive. If your laptop is running slowly to boot up, freezing when opening normal applications or frequently showing a loading circle then further investigation is required.

Begin by restarting your laptop and updating any pending OS and application updates from a trusted source. Disable any unnecessary startup programs. Delete any unneeded files and ensure important documents and photos are backed up separately. Check Task Manager (Windows) or Activity Monitor (Mac) to see which applications are using an unusual amount of CPU, Memory or Disk.

By completing these steps you should see an improvement. However if your laptop is still running slowly a technician can investigate the health of your drive, memory, cooling and any errors in the Operating System. Upgrading to a solid state drive instead of a traditional hard disk drive can significantly improve the performance of a compatible laptop. Increasing the memory can also help if you frequently use multiple applications. However the right solution depends on your laptop model, specification and the tasks you require.

content.heading: 3. Battery Life / Charging Issues
paragraphs: The battery in your laptop will reduce as they age. If you’re noticing your battery isn’t lasting long when fully charged, dropping rapidly or shutting down when disconnected then your battery may be worn. Charging issues can also occur due to a damaged cable, loose charging port, incorrect charger or power issues.

Check if your battery level is increasing when plugged into the correct charger. Check the charging cable and charger for any visible damage, excessive heat or loose connections. Ensure you are using the correct charger for your specific model and do not force the connector into the charging port. If your laptop supports it you can check the health of the battery and see how much charge is left and how many charge cycles it has completed.

A technician can investigate the health of your charger, charging port and battery. If your battery requires replacing then ensure you use a compatible quality battery to be fitted safely. If your battery is swelling then this is a serious issue. Stop using and charging your laptop and do not press or puncture the battery. Arrange for a professional service to be completed as soon as possible. Never throw away any damaged lithium ion batteries.

content.heading: 4. Unusual Sounds / Freezing / Unexpected Shutdowns
paragraphs: Unusual clicking, grinding or rattling sounds shouldn’t be ignored. Some laptops use a mechanical hard drive which can cause noise if there is an issue. The fan can also cause a rattling noise if there is an obstruction or damage. However modern laptops use solid state drives with no moving parts so the clicking is more likely to be from another component.

If your laptop is frequently freezing, displaying blue screens, randomly restarting or unexpectedly shutting down it could be due to overheating, memory issues, storage issues, corrupt drivers, power issues or other hardware issues. Make a note of when the issue is occurring and any error messages displayed. If your laptop is still working back up any important files to an external drive or trusted cloud. If your laptop is becoming unstable then you should not rely on it as your only copy.

Avoid forcing your laptop to restart if there are unusual noises coming from your drive. A professional can investigate the memory, storage, cooling and power components. Identifying an issue early can help prevent a small issue turning into a more costly repair and help keep your data safe.

content.heading: 5. Keyboard, Screen, Ports or Other Issues
paragraphs: Not all hardware issues are major. You may be noticing individual keys aren’t working, the touchpad is acting strangely, the screen is flickering or your USB and charging ports are loose. You may also notice dead pixels, lines on your screen, distorted sound or your webcam is no longer being detected.

Start by removing any external accessories, restarting your laptop and ensuring you have the correct input / display settings. If your external monitor is working but your laptop screen isn’t then there could be an issue with the screen, cable or graphics. If only one USB isn’t working try plugging another known working device into another port.

Do not force the USB plug in, press hard on a broken screen or attempt to clean your keyboard with liquid cleaners. If you have had a spill then take extra care. Turn the laptop off and if possible unplug the power. Seek professional advice. By powering on a device with liquid damage you are increasing the risk of corrosion or short circuits. A technician can identify if a component can be repaired or needs replacing.

content.heading: What can be done during a professional laptop service?
paragraphs: During a service a technician may check the exterior, internal dust, cooling, fan and temperature, storage health, memory, battery & charging, OS and basic keyboard, screen, ports, camera & sound. The exact tasks will depend on the condition of your laptop and symptoms.

Before handing over your laptop ensure you have backed up any important files. Make a note of the condition of your laptop and clearly describe any symptoms. Ask what they will be checking, if any parts are original or compatible, the estimated cost and if there is a service warranty. Avoid sharing your passwords. If they do need to access your laptop for testing then discuss setting up a temporary account.

content.heading: How to minimise unexpected repairs
paragraphs: Place your laptop on a clean firm surface and ensure there is plenty of space around the ventilation. Wipe the outside using the correct cleaning products and a soft cloth. Ensure your OS and security software is up to date, use reliable security software, avoid downloading anything suspicious and ensure you have regular backups. Avoid eating or drinking near your laptop and place in a padded bag. Avoid tugging the charging cable.

Whilst good habits won’t stop all hardware issues they can help reduce any unnecessary damage and make it easier to identify issues. Checking your laptop periodically can be very helpful if regularly used for business, learning or high demand tasks.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Overheating, slow performance, bad battery life, unusual noises and hardware issues are 5 key indicators that your laptop may need some maintenance. Don’t wait until it completely fails. Back up your data, make a note of any symptoms and book in a qualified technician. Performing maintenance can improve the reliability of your laptop and keep your valuable data safe.

Printerworld can be a great contact point for your laptop and printer needs. Ensure you know what services can be provided, what they will be doing to diagnose, the estimated cost and warranty for your specific device.

title: Inkjet vs Laser Printer: Which Is Right for You?
seoTitle: Inkjet vs Laser Printer: Which Is Right for You?
metaDescription: Compare inkjet and laser printers by print quality, speed, running costs, maintenance and use case to choose the right printer for home or office.
excerpt: Compare inkjet and laser printers by print quality, speed, running costs, maintenance and use case to choose the right printer for home or office.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: When looking to choose a printer there are quite a few things to consider such as technology type, cartridges, print speed and cost. Inkjet and laser are the two most common types available. However, whilst they can both produce useful documents they both work in different ways.

An inkjet printer works by using very small drops of liquid ink to create an image on the paper. Laser printers work by using electro-photographic technology. This means the laser/LED creates an image on a photosensitive drum. Toner powder is then transferred to the paper and bonded using heat. This will affect the quality, speed, servicing and cost.
There is no one right choice, it really depends on what you want to print, how often you want to print, whether you need colour and how much you want to spend.

content.heading: Inkjet Printers
paragraphs: Inkjet printers use either ink cartridges or ink tanks to print. The printhead sprays very small amounts of ink onto the paper. Many printers have separate black and colour cartridge’s. Others may have refillable ink tanks. Inkjet technology is very versatile and is a popular choice for printing at home, school projects, pictures and colour documents.

A benefit of using an inkjet printer is that they can produce clear, colourful images with smooth shading. They are also available in compact sizes at an affordable price. Some have the added bonus of having scanning and copying facilities.

However, as ink is liquid it can dry out around the printhead if you leave them unused for long periods. Cleaning cycles can use up ink. On some models they can be quite expensive to replace the cartridges. Paper can also be an issue as some may not absorb the ink as well as special photo paper.

content.heading: Laser Printers
paragraphs: Laser printers use toner (a fine powder) instead of liquid ink. An image is created on a drum and the toner is attracted to the correct areas. It is then transferred to the paper and fixed using heat to create a finished document. This means they can produce documents quickly.

They are a great choice for offices, schools and homes that print large amounts of text. They often print in black and white quickly. If you don’t need high quality images and are looking for predictable document printing they can be a good choice. As toner is not liquid it won’t dry out like ink can be.

Laser printers can be more expensive to purchase especially if you want colour. They can also be larger and heavier than entry level inkjet printers. Whilst colour laser printing can be great for many charts, presentations and documents, if you want high quality images for photos an inkjet specifically for photos may be a better choice.

content.heading: Quality of print - Documents, Graphics & Photographs
paragraphs: Both inkjet and laser printers can be a good choice if you’re printing normal documents such as letters, invoices, assignments and reports. A good quality laser printer can often produce very clear black text. Inkjet printers can also produce clear documents if the printhead and paper settings are in good condition.

When printing photos inkjet printers tend to be more versatile. They are often a preferred choice for those wanting vibrant colours, shading and detailed images. How well they print will depend on the resolution, ink, paper and colour settings. Not all inkjet printers will be photo printers so make sure to look at sample prints and specifications.

For business graphics it will depend on what you want to print. Laser printers can be a good choice for charts, forms and coloured reports. Inkjet printers can also be a good choice for posters, images and mixed media depending on the model. If you need accurate colour make sure to check what media is supported, colour system and profiles.

content.heading: Print Speed & Volume
paragraphs: Laser printers are often a good choice for large volumes of text. Many business models are designed to handle high volumes of work with relatively high print speeds. Inkjet printers can vary greatly. Entry level printers may be slower. However some business models can be designed to print documents quickly.

Don’t just look at the print speed. Depending on the mode (draft, standard or high quality) the printer may have different print speeds. The first page may also take longer to print. Look for printers with a recommended monthly print volume. This will give you a better idea of how they will perform in regular use.

If you don’t print a lot of pages a month you may not need a high volume printer. For example if you’re a family printing occasional forms and school assignments. If you’re a small office printing invoices, reports and customer documents daily make sure to look at how many sheets of paper can be held, duplex printing, network connection and cost of consumables.

content.heading: Cost - Cartridges/Toner
paragraphs: When looking at the cost of a printer you need to consider how much it will cost to replace the ink/toner, drum (if applicable), servicing parts, paper and electricity. The number of pages printed using the cartridge/toner is usually calculated using standardised testing. This can vary depending on how much of the page is covered, mode, type of documents being printed and how they are used.

Ink tank printers may be a good choice if you print a lot. They can be more expensive to purchase but the cost per page can be lower. Ink cartridge printers can be affordable to purchase but may be more expensive to run if the cartridges are expensive or have a low page yield. Laser printers can have a higher page yield for text based documents. However make sure to check if the toner cartridge includes the drum or if it is a separate item.

Make sure to look at how much genuine and approved consumables will cost for that exact model. If you go for a cheap printer but the consumables are expensive or hard to find it can get expensive. Work out roughly how much they will cost per month depending on how many pages you expect to print.

content.heading: Servicing
paragraphs: Inkjet printers may need servicing such as cleaning the printhead. If you don’t use them for long periods of time follow the manufacturers guidelines on turning on, servicing and storing the cartridges. Don’t keep running the cleaning function if the output isn’t great as this will waste ink.

Laser printers won’t have liquid ink to dry out however they will still need servicing. Toner cartridges, drums, rollers and fuser all have a service life. Using dusty paper, incorrect paper and heavy use can cause issues with feeding paper through and quality of the print. Both should be stored in a clean and dry place. Use the correct paper and consumables.
Depending on the model, amount of use, environment and servicing the reliability can vary. Make sure to look at the warranty, local servicing and cost of replacement parts.

content.heading: Which Printer?
paragraphs: If you regularly print colour photos, creative documents or mixed documents an inkjet printer would be a good choice. If you have a household or small business that prints a lot of colour an ink tank model may be a good choice. If you don’t print often and want something affordable an ink cartridge may be enough.

If you mainly print text, print a lot, want fast printing or want something that can sit unused for a while without the liquid ink drying out a laser printer would be a good choice. If you’re an office that rarely need colour a mono laser printer can be a good choice. If you’re an office that prints charts, brochures and presentations a colour laser may be a good choice. Make sure to check how well the colour prints and cost of consumables.

Before purchasing make sure to look at what connections it has, automatic duplex printing, how many sheets of paper it can hold, print speed, scanning capabilities, what operating systems it works with, size and warranty. If you have more than one person using it make sure it has network/Wi-Fi.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Both inkjet and laser printers have different purposes. Inkjet printers often have an appealing factor for photos and versatile colour printing. Laser printers often are a great choice for quick, regular document printing. The best choice will depend on what you actually need the printer for and the overall cost.

Make a list of what you need to print, how many pages you print a month and if you need colour, scanning and duplex printing. Compare different models and consumables. Printerworld can help customers find the right printer for their needs and what servicing they may need. Make sure the model you choose is available, consumables are compatible and what servicing is offered.

title: How to Choose the Right Laptop for Your Needs
seoTitle: How to Choose the Right Laptop for Your Needs
metaDescription: A practical laptop buying guide covering purpose, processor, RAM, storage, display, battery, portability, connectivity and budget.
excerpt: A practical laptop buying guide covering purpose, processor, RAM, storage, display, battery, portability, connectivity and budget.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Purchasing a laptop is a big commitment and it can become a valuable tool in your daily routine. Whether you're a student using your laptop for classes, assignments or research, or a professional using it for documents, meetings and specialist software – or even a creative needing a powerful processor, memory and graphics – you want a device that will fit your needs.

However, there is quite a lot to think about when looking at the specs of a laptop. It can become overwhelming deciding between different models with different processors, amounts of RAM, storage, screen and battery. The best laptop for you won't necessarily be the most expensive one or the one with the longest list of specs. Rather it should be one that will easily handle your tasks, fit within your budget and will be able to get support.
To help you decide:

content.heading: 1. Tasks
paragraphs: Write down what you will be using your laptop for. If you're just using it for basic tasks such as browsing, emailing, video calls and word processing then an entry level or mid range laptop might be fine. If you're a student using office software, learning platforms and research tools then you'll generally benefit from having a responsive processor, sufficient memory and an SSD.

If you're going to be using it for programming, data analysis or multitasking then you may want to consider a more powerful processor and more RAM. As a developer you should look into the requirements of your IDE, virtual machines, containers and any other tools you use. If you're using it for graphic design, video editing, 3D or gaming you might need a graphics card, colourful display and more memory.

If you're using specialist software for your profession then always check the official requirements for that software. Whilst you may be able to run the software on a laptop that meets the minimum requirements, it will run much better if it meets the recommended specs. Don't waste money on a high spec gaming laptop if you won't actually need it for your everyday tasks.

content.heading: 2. Processor
paragraphs: The processor (CPU) is responsible for running general computing tasks. The performance of the processor will affect how quickly your applications run and how well it will handle high intensity tasks. It's a good idea to look at the family and generation of the processor.

Modern entry and mid range processors can be very capable for everyday use. However, if you're doing more intensive tasks then you might want to look for a higher performance range of processors with more cores and a better sustained performance. You should also consider the energy efficiency of the processor, as this will affect how hot it gets, how noisy the fan will be and how long the battery will last.

Try to look up unbiased reviews for that exact spec of laptop. Even if two laptops have similar sounding processors they can have different performances due to the cooling solution, power and memory. Sometimes a laptop with a well designed cooling solution can have a better sustained performance than a slim laptop with a faster processor.

content.heading: 3. RAM
paragraphs: RAM is used as a short term memory for your applications and OS. If your laptop doesn't have lots of RAM available it can cause it to use more from your storage, meaning you may experience a laggy performance when trying to multitask. If you're using lots of open tabs in your web browser along with office software, communication tools and other tools then you may benefit from more RAM.For basic tasks a low spec of RAM may be fine. However, if you're doing more intensive tasks or using modern applications then 8GB can feel tight. Many users will find it more comfortable to have 16GB RAM to allow them to run their general productivity, studying or development tasks. If you're a creative professional or using virtual machines then you might need 32GB or more depending on the software you're using.
Check if the RAM is upgradable or soldered to the motherboard. If it's soldered then you may be stuck with that amount of RAM. Choose an amount that will suit your future needs.

content.heading: 4. SSD Storage
paragraphs: Most new laptops will be best considered with a solid state drive (SSD). This will give you faster access to your OS, applications and files. This can help speed up your boot time, application loading and overall performance.

You'll also want to consider the size of your storage. If you're using it for light use and storing your files in the cloud then 256GB may be enough. However, once you start installing applications, media and project files it can fill up quickly. A 512GB SSD will be more flexible for many users. If you're working with large video, design or research files then you may need 1TB or more. Or have a reliable backup plan for external storage.
Check if your laptop has upgradable storage. Don't forget to back up your data.

content.heading: 5. Screen Size & Display
paragraphs: Laptops come in various sizes. Smaller laptops are easier to carry around but larger screens can give you more space to work with. If you're travelling a lot then a 13" or 14" laptop can give you a good balance. If you're mostly using your laptop at your desk then a 15" or 16" may be a better option.

The resolution, brightness, viewing angles, colours, refresh rate and finish will all affect the performance of your screen. A full HD screen will be a good starting point for many users. Creatives should consider the colours more. If you're working outdoors or in bright rooms then you may need a brighter screen with an anti glare finishIf possible try to view the screen in person. Check how comfortable the text looks at your preferred scaling and if the hinge and viewing angles are comfortable.

content.heading: 6. Battery Life
paragraphs: The battery life will depend on the battery size, processor, screen, software, tasks and settings. The advertised battery life from the manufacturer will usually be based on testing in controlled environments. This can vary greatly when using your laptop for video calls, high screen brightness, gaming and high intensity applications.

Look for reviews that have tested the battery life in realistic situations. Check if the laptop can be charged using USB-C. Also check how many watts the adapter is and if it can be charged using a compatible power bank. A fast charging feature can be useful but shouldn't be the main factor.

If you're a student or travelling professional then the weight and size of the charger can be very important. Even if it has a great battery life it may be inconvenient if the power adapter is unusually heavy.

content.heading: 7. Keyboard, Touchpad, Webcam & Sound
paragraphs: Whilst looking at the specs it's also important to consider the keyboard. If you're typing a lot then having a comfortable keyboard with well spaced keys and useful travel can make a big difference. Check if the keyboard is well laid out, has a good layout for function keys and has a backlit keyboard. You'll also want a responsive and accurate touchpad.

If you're using your laptop for online classes or meetings then you should look at the webcam resolution, microphone quality and speakers. Having noise cancellation and a good webcam position can make you look more professional whilst on calls. If you're using a headset or external mic then check if there are enough ports.

The build quality can also be important. Ensure it has a sturdy hinge, solid keyboard and feels like it's made from the right materials for the intended use. If you're using it daily then it should be designed to handle normal use.

content.heading: 8. Ports, Connectivity & Compatibility
paragraphs: Work out what devices you'll be connecting to your laptop. External monitors, USB drives, printers, projectors, memory cards, wired network and sound devices. Check how many ports there are and what type. USB-A, USB-C, HDMI, Audio and Ethernet if needed. Some slim laptops may only have a few ports so you may need to invest in a hub or docking station.

Check the laptop has Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Also ensure it's compatible with your OS. Check if your printer or other peripherals have the correct drivers. If you're planning on using two external monitors then ensure the laptop can output to multiple displays.

content.heading: 9. Set a Budget & Value for Money
paragraphs: Before browsing set a budget. Work out what you can't compromise on. Look at laptops with similar amounts of RAM, Storage and Screen. The advertised price may not be for the same spec as in the picture.

Consider how long the warranty lasts, how easy it is to get to a service centre, if it has accidental damage cover, how much it will cost to upgrade and if the essential accessories are included. A slightly higher priced laptop with a good build quality and local support may be a better value for money in the long run.
Don't waste money on features you won't be using. Invest in the parts that will directly affect your work.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Understanding what you'll be using your laptop for will help you pick the right one for you. Ensure it has the right processor, RAM, storage, screen, battery and connectivity for your most used tasks. Check the exact spec, warranty and if it can be upgraded. Try to look up reviews for that specific model.

A good laptop should be suitable for your current needs without becoming frustrating. We can help our customers consider what laptop would be best for them alongside their printer and accessory needs. Ensure the laptop you're looking at has the right specs, is available and has good after sales support.

content.heading: Think about the lifespan
paragraphs: When choosing your laptop you should think about how long you would expect to use it. Check what warranty the manufacturer is offering. How easy it is to get to an authorised service. How much common parts such as a battery, keyboard and charger would cost to replace. If it has upgradable storage it can be easier to upgrade as your files increase. However, if it's a slim laptop with soldered memory you may still find it suitable if you choose enough RAM. Ensure the OS will be supported for long enough. Also ensure it meets the requirements of any applications you're likely to use in the coming years. If you need it to be portable then consider the actual weight of the laptop and power adapter. A comfortable keyboard, sturdy hinge and good webcam can make you happier using your laptop daily.

title: 5 Common Laptop Problems and How to Deal With Them
seoTitle: 5 Common Laptop Problems and How to Deal With Them
metaDescription: Discover five common laptop problems and practical first steps for troubleshooting slow performance, overheating, battery, Wi-Fi and startup issues.
excerpt: Discover five common laptop problems and practical first steps for troubleshooting slow performance, overheating, battery, Wi-Fi and startup issues.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Sometimes even a reliable laptop can have issues. The issue could be caused by something simple like a disconnected cable or just an application using too many resources. Other issues could be caused by a degrade battery, blockage within the cooling system, faulty storage or a faulty part.

Be sure to back up any data on your laptop and avoid doing anything that could worsen your issue. If your laptop is still under warranty, before attempting to open it up or take it to an unauthorised repair centre, read through the manufacturers support advice. The following are 5 common issues that can occur and the safe steps you can take to address the issue and decide whether to take to a professional.

content.heading: Slow laptop
paragraphs: A slow laptop can cause long start up times, freezing between apps or struggling while using multiple browsers. Causes could include too many start up applications, not enough RAM, not enough storage space, background updates, malware or overheating.

First give the laptop a normal restart. Ensure you save anything you are working on and close any unnecessary applications. Check what is using your CPU, RAM or storage. Use Task manager on Windows or Activity monitor on Mac to see what is using a lot of resources. Turn off any unnecessary start ups, uninstall any applications you no longer use and ensure you have the latest OS.

Ensure you have enough storage space. Don’t delete any strange folders on your system or use any unknown registry cleaners. Run a scan using a reputable security programme. If your laptop is still slow, a technician can run tests on your storage, RAM and cooling. Upgrading to an SSD or increasing your memory could help.

content.heading: Overheating laptop
paragraphs: An overheating laptop can be uncomfortable, cause noisy fans and cause a drop in performance. Causes could include dust build up, blocked vents, faulty fan, high processor usage or the laptop not being on a suitable surface.

Place your laptop on a solid flat surface. Ensure there is no blockage to your vents. Avoid placing it on a bed, sofa or cushion. Close any unnecessary applications. Check if anything is causing your processor to work hard. If your fan is working very hard when doing simple tasks or frequently shutting down, book an inspection.

Avoid using a domestic vacuum on any parts inside, inserting anything into the vents or opening up the laptop if you don’t have the appropriate experience. You may need to be careful when opening up your laptop to clean the inside. Some laptops have fragile cables or small cooling units. A technician can clean out the fan and heatsink and check that there is good airflow.

content.heading: Battery not charging or fast drain
paragraphs: A laptop battery can degrade over time however issues with charging can be caused by the charger, cable, port or power management. Ensure you are using the correct charger for your laptop and it is fully plugged in. Check that there is no damage to the cable or charger. Try plugging into a different suitable socket on the wall.

If your laptop is acknowledging the charger but not increasing the battery % check using the battery health tool from the manufacturer or battery report from the OS. Some laptops have battery saver mode which will limit the charging to help the long term health of the battery. This could be normal.

Reduce brightness, close any unnecessary applications and check what is running in the background. If your laptop is frequently turning off, the battery % is spiking or the battery looks swollen, stop using it and contact a professional. Don’t try to poke, bend or press the swollen battery.

content.heading: No Wi-Fi / Internet
paragraphs: If your laptop isn’t connecting to Wi-Fi this could be due to an issue with the router, incorrect password, Wi-Fi turned off, outdated drivers, network settings or hardware issues. Firstly check other devices can connect. If none can, try restarting the router as per your internet providers instructions. Check for any service outages.

If other devices are working, turn Wi-Fi off then on again. Ensure Airplane mode is switched off. Connect to the right network. Be careful when entering your password. Restart your laptop and update any network drivers from the official support page of your laptop manufacturer. Don’t download drivers from unknown sites.

If your laptop is connecting to Wi-Fi but the websites aren’t loading, try a different website. Check if a VPN or Proxy is causing an issue. Try forgetting the network and reconnecting. Make a note of your password. If there is no wireless adapter showing in your system settings or it keeps dropping the connection on different networks you may need a professional to diagnose.

content.heading: Laptop won’t turn on
paragraphs: If your laptop seems to be completely dead this could be due to a dead battery, faulty charger, damaged charging port, stuck power state or internal hardware issues. Firstly complete a safe visual check. Remove any unnecessary peripherals. Plug in the correct charger into a known working socket. Check for any charging indicators. Let it charge for a while.

Complete the power reset procedure suggested by your manufacturers. This will vary depending on your model so make sure you follow the correct instructions for your laptop. If it has any external peripherals that can be removed, remove these. See if there are any lights, fan spin or any sounds when powering on. This can help a technician identify the issue.

If there is any burning smell, liquid damage, strange heating or the battery looks swollen, safely unplug the power. Don’t try to open up the power adapter or attempt any motherboard repairs. A qualified technician can test the charger, battery, power port, memory and mainboard.

content.heading: When to stop trying to fix the issue
paragraphs: If your laptop has suffered any liquid damage, the battery is swollen, the charger or port look damaged, there is a burning smell, or it keeps turning off, stop trying to fix the issue. If you think important files are at risk due to storage failure, or after basic checks the issue hasn’t been resolved and would require the laptop to be opened, contact a professional.

Trying random fixes can make it harder to diagnose. Make a note of any symptoms, error codes, any recent changes and what you have tried. This can help a service professional identify what the likely cause is quicker.

content.heading: Ways to prevent issues with your laptop
paragraphs: Ensure you keep your software updated through official sources. Keep a good security programme. Regularly back up important files. Ensure nothing is blocking your vents. Use a padded laptop bag when transporting. Avoid eating or drinking over the keyboard. Be careful when removing any peripherals. Use the correct charger. Shut down or restart when needed.

Don’t ignore minor changes. If your fan is getting louder, battery is draining quicker or there are new errors on start up this could be a sign of an issue starting to develop. Fixing the symptoms early can reduce downtime and repair costs.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Common issues users face with their laptop are slowness, overheating, battery issues, Wi-Fi issues and not turning on. Some of these issues can be fixed by completing some safe checks. However if there is an hardware issue or signs such as swelling, liquid damage or burning smell then a professional should be contacted.

Ensure you back up your files. Follow the official support instructions and don’t open it up if you aren’t qualified. If the issue still isn’t resolved book a proper diagnosis so the root cause can be addressed.

title: 7 Simple Ways to Maintain Your Printer
seoTitle: 7 Simple Ways to Maintain Your Printer
metaDescription: Keep your printer reliable with seven practical maintenance habits covering cleaning, paper, cartridges, software, placement and regular use.
excerpt: Keep your printer reliable with seven practical maintenance habits covering cleaning, paper, cartridges, software, placement and regular use.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Printers can be very easy to forget about. They sit quietly on your desk or office. However, when problems occur such as streaky prints, paper jams and connectivity issues it can cause a huge disruption to your whole day.

Performing some basic maintenance can help prevent problems and keep your printer running smoothly. The exact maintenance will depend on what type of printer you have (ink jet, ink tank or laser). Always refer to the manufacturers guide for your printer model. Here are 7 key tips to keep your home or office printers running smoothly.

content.heading: 1. Clean the outside
paragraphs: Over time dust, paper fibres and debris can build up on your printer. Turn the printer off and unplug before cleaning. Refer to the safety guidelines provided by the manufacturer. Use a soft lint free cloth and dampen slightly. Do not spray any liquid directly onto your printer.

Avoid using harsh chemicals, abrasive cloths and too much pressure on buttons, screens and labels. If you are able to clean certain rollers or areas of your printer refer to the manufacturers guidelines. Try not to get too deep into your printer or touch any hot parts on your laser printer.
Try to keep your printer away from too much dust, moisture, heat and cooking areas. This will help to stop debris entering the printer.

content.heading: 2. Use the right paper
paragraphs: The quality of your paper will directly affect how well your printer feeds and your results. Use the correct paper size, weight and type. Using damp, curled, torn or very crumpled paper can cause paper jams.

Store your paper flat in its original packaging and in a dry place. Ensure the edges are neat and only fan the paper if the manufacturers guide says so. Don’t overfill the paper tray. Ensure the paper guides are adjusted to sit just touching the paper without causing it to bend.

If you are printing on photo paper, labels, envelopes or thick paper ensure you have selected the correct paper setting and paper feed. Incorrect settings can cause bad quality prints, smudging and feeding issues. Remove the unused paper if the environment is humid or dusty.

content.heading: 3. Ink & Toner
paragraphs: Ink and toner cartridges are specific to your printer model. Ensure you know the exact model number and consumable code. If you haven’t opened the ink/toner yet store them as per the manufacturers guidelines. Keep them away from extreme heat and direct sunlight.

Ink jet printers – Avoid touching the electrical contacts and nozzles. Only remove cartridges if you are changing or maintaining. If the printer is showing low ink warnings refer to the manufacturers guidelines. Ink tank printers will have specific refilling instructions. Ensure you use the right type of ink and don’t overfill.

Laser printers – Be careful with your toner. Refer to the manufacturers guidelines. Avoid shaking the toner too much as it is a fine powder. Avoid touching the sensitive drums. If you spill toner refer to the manufacturers guidelines.

content.heading: 4. Print/Service the printer
paragraphs: Some ink jet printers can suffer from dry ink and clogged nozzles if they sit for long periods. If you only print occasionally refer to the manufacturers guidelines. Printing a small test page can help identify print quality issues. However try not to clean the printer unnecessarily as it will waste ink.

Laser printers do not use liquid ink so the toner will not dry. However, they will still benefit from being kept clean and using the correct paper. If you share the printer between a team ensure it isn’t getting too dusty.
The aim is not to print unnecessary pages. Just follow the service guidelines for your printer model.

content.heading: 5. Update software/drivers
paragraphs: Sometimes printers will seem broken due to driver issues. Always download drivers and firmware from the official manufacturers site. Ensure you know the exact model and operating system.

If your printer has stopped printing after updating your computer check it is still the default printer. Check it has the correct driver. If it is a network printer check both devices are on the correct network. Avoid removing old or duplicate printers unless you know what printer you are using.
Updating firmware can help with compatibility and resolving known issues. Follow the manufacturers guidelines. Do not turn off your printer.

content.heading: 6. Avoid paper jams
paragraphs: Paper jams are often caused by incorrect paper, overfilled trays, incorrect paper guides and small pieces of paper. Always follow the manufacturer guidelines. Turn the printer off if prompted and gently remove paper. Don’t tug the paper as it can cause it to tear.

Only open the covers that are meant to be opened. Don’t force paper through the rollers or touch the hot fuser. If the paper tears, the printer keeps jamming or the rollers are making strange noises then arrange for service. If it keeps jamming in the same area then it could be a sign of worn rollers.

content.heading: 7. Position & Ventilation
paragraphs: Ensure your printer is on a stable surface and has enough space for the trays and covers to open. Ensure there is enough ventilation around the printer. Don’t put it in a tight cabinet unless the manufacturer say it is ok. Avoid direct sunlight, heaters, water and heavy dust areas.

If you are using your printer in an office environment think about where you are putting it. Ensure any cables aren’t a problem and you can easily replace paper and maintain. If it is hard to reach then it may be mishandled or the jams not resolved. Ensure you have a suitable power point and don’t have any unsafe extension cords. If it is on a network ensure it has the correct security settings and the software is up to date.

content.heading: Basic Printer Maintenance Tips
paragraphs: To make it as simple as possible, weekly check the paper. Remove any small bits of paper and wipe down any obvious dust. When replacing any cartridges or toner check the area and follow the manufacturers guidelines. If your print quality is suffering use the nozzle clean, align or calibrate tools. Check for driver updates and any maintenance messages.

Businesses who tend to print a lot should keep a log of when you service the printer. Include your printer model, how many pages printed (if possible), what consumables have been changed, any error messages and when it was serviced. This can help identify any ongoing issues. You can plan to service your printer in advance.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: You don’t need to over complicate printer maintenance. Keeping it clean, using the right paper, being careful with your consumables, following the manufacturers guidelines for your model, keeping your software up to date and clearing jams safely will help to keep your printer running smoothly.

If your printer is constantly jamming, printing badly or showing errors don’t force it to work. Get a professional to check it out to see if any parts are worn. Printerworld can help support customers with choosing the right printer, consumables and servicing. Find out what services are available for your model.

title: why regular Printer servicing is important for businesses.
seoTitle: why regular Printer servicing is important for businesses
metaDescription: Understand why regular business printer servicing reduces downtime, improves print quality, controls costs and supports a productive workplace.
excerpt: Understand why regular business printer servicing reduces downtime, improves print quality, controls costs and supports a productive workplace.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Printers are still very much used in many businesses. Team members will use printers to print important documents like invoices, contracts, reports, delivery documents, labels, presentations and customer records. If you have a printer that is not functioning properly, staff may be wasting time trying to fix the issue. This can cause delays to key documentation and cause disruption to customer facing tasks. If the printer is not looked after, you may start to see a loss in productivity for your business.

Regular printer maintenance allows you to service your printer. This means you can check the printer, ensure it is cleaned and the correct parts are in stock. You can check for wear and tear and fix any small issues. Depending on the printer type, age, usage, environment and manufacturers advice you will need to service your printer regularly. If you use your printer regularly throughout the day, regular maintenance can be more practical.

content.heading: 1. Reduce downtime
paragraphs: Issues with your printer are rarely convenient. If your printer is having an issue feeding paper, causing problems with your toner or causing network issues whilst you are busy during month end invoicing, this will cause a delay to multiple people. If you only have one printer in your business, a short downtime can cause a queue to build up.

By having a regular maintenance schedule, you can get a technician to check your printer. You can ensure paper feed rollers, separation pads, accessible areas, sensors and other parts are checked. This will allow you to identify any early signs of wear and tear. Whilst not all issues can be avoided, having a service history will allow you to identify any regular issues. Having your printer serviced regularly will allow you to ensure you have the correct consumables in stock. You will also be able to plan to have support in place ahead of a known busy time. You can also consider if you need an extra printer or print solution for key workflows.

content.heading: 2. Improve print quality
paragraphs: Having poor print quality can cause you to look unprofessional. Poor print quality can cause issues with faded text, streaks, spots, inconsistent colours, smudging and repeating lines. This can cause issues with reading documents. All important documents such as invoices, forms, proposals and labels should have good quality and consistency.

There can be multiple reasons why print quality is poor. Inkjet printers may need a check of nozzles, alignment and cleaning as advised by the manufacturer. Laser printers may need a check of toner, drum units, transfer, rollers and fuser. Issues can also be caused by incorrect paper, incorrect media settings and poor quality consumables.

A service professional can check using test pages and diagnostics. You don’t want to be replacing parts unnecessarily so you want to identify the root cause. If you keep samples of poor print you can also identify the issue quicker. Note if it is affecting all pages, just colour or certain papers.

content.heading: 3. Reduce total printing costs
paragraphs: When purchasing a printer there are many costs to consider. Along with the initial purchase price you will also be paying for ink/toner, drums (if applicable), paper, parts, electricity, repair and staff time. If your printer is not looked after you may be causing wastage due to repeated cleaning, paper jams, test prints and needing to reprint.

Having your printer serviced can help identify any issues that may be increasing your running costs. Worn rollers can cause repeated paper jams. Incorrect settings can cause colour printing unnecessarily. If your printer is not set up for double sided printing you may be using more paper than needed. If your printer isn’t suited to the volume you print each month you may have frequent service interruptions or need to replace your printer earlier than expected.

You should consider the cost per page, consumable yield and volume you actually print each month. If you have a department that prints a lot you may want to invest in a model that can handle increased volumes. Your service provider can help you decide if it is more cost effective to repair, replace, adjust settings or change the type of printer. Consider the age of the device, estimated repair cost, availability of parts and expected future volume.

content.heading: 4. Increase lifespan
paragraphs: Printers have lots of moving parts and will naturally suffer from wear and tear. Paper rollers spin, trays open and close and internal parts can cause heat, pressure and mechanical movement. Dust and paper can build up especially if your printer is used frequently. If not looked after properly, small issues can cause frequent paper jams, inconsistent feeding and unnecessary stress on the device.

Preventative maintenance will focus on the areas as advised by the manufacturer. This can include cleaning the correct accessible areas, checking paper path, service messages, rollers and ensuring your printer is operating within it’s intended volume. Laser printers can have a range of maintenance parts such as drums and fusers. These will have a service life depending on the model. Inkjet printers have different requirements, especially for printheads.

Not all printers will need servicing at the same frequency. If you have a printer that isn’t used much in your home office you may need to service it less frequently than a multi-functional printer for your whole department. Follow the manufacturers advice and consider the volume you print each month, paper quality and any previous issues. Do not open any covers or touch any hot or sensitive parts unless stated in the manual.

content.heading: 5. Improve productivity in the workplace
paragraphs: If you have a printer that is shared amongst staff members they will have to leave their desk to find another printer, reprint and/or contact IT. If you have frequent issues this can cause a lot of interruptions.

Having a reliable printer will improve your workflow. Staff members can print when needed, departments can meet deadlines and your IT team can spend their time on high value tasks instead of fixing the same printer issues. Having your printer set up correctly can also help you with secure printing, network access, scanning to approved locations and efficient double sided printing.

Consider how you have your printers set up. If your printer isn’t in a convenient location for your teams you may have unnecessary movement. If too many people are using your printer it could be overworked. If you have clear guidelines for paper loading, tray selection and error reporting this will help stop any unnecessary misuse. Printer servicing will work best if you have them in a logical location, with clear guidelines and correct setup.

content.heading: 6. Help with security and reliable connectivity
paragraphs: Printers are networked devices and may contain information about your print jobs, address book, network details and more. Using a service will help you to check your printer has the correct firmware and configuration. Ensure you have strong admin details, limit unnecessary access and follow your IT team’s network security policy.

Sometimes issues with your printer can be caused by connectivity issues. Your printer may be in good condition but having issues accessing it due to the IP address changing, driver issues, wireless or print queue issues. Your service provider or IT admin can check your connectivity, drivers and access. Ensure firmware updates are coming directly from the manufacturer and are carried out as per the official guidelines. Take the correct precautions to avoid disruption.

Before your technician accesses your network printer ensure you have clarity on what level of access is required and follow your internal processes. Avoid showing any passwords or sensitive document details in your service history. Agree who is responsible for security.

content.heading: 7. Create a printer maintenance schedule
paragraphs: Your printer maintenance schedule doesn’t need to be complicated. You should start by noting the printer model, serial number, location, date installed and approximate monthly volume. Note what consumables the printer uses, warranty status and any regular error messages. This will help you to understand which printers are key to your business and which are suitable for replacement.

Create a simple schedule based on the manufacturers advice and actual usage. Simple checks can be done by staff members to ensure paper is loaded correctly, area is clean and any regular errors reported. Any technical work should be carried out by an authorised or qualified service professional. Keep track of when your printer was serviced, what parts were replaced, what consumables were used and any issues noted.

Ensure you have a process in place for urgent issues. Ensure your staff know who to contact, what information to provide and if they need to reprint on another printer. Consider having a backup device for critical printing. Regularly review your schedule as your business grows and printing changes.

content.heading: Choosing a printer service
paragraphs: A good service provider will be able to explain what checks they will carry out, what the likely costs will be, what parts will be required and how long it will take. Ask if they can service your exact model, if they have spare parts and what warranty they offer on completed work. If you have multiple devices ask if they can keep track of your assets and service history.

Ensure they communicate well. Before approving any repairs ask for a diagnosis and estimate. Ensure you know if the estimate includes labour, parts, delivery and tax. Ask what will happen if further issues are found. Ensure you understand if they will need to have access to data, network or security.

Don’t always go for the cheapest quote. Consider technical ability, quick response, transparency, quality of parts and their ability to support your operational needs. Printerworld can help you with your printer support, supplies and repair. Ensure they can support your exact models and services.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Regular printer servicing can help to reduce unnecessary downtime, ensure you have clear print quality, control your running costs and ensure your printer is in good working condition. It can also help to improve productivity by reducing frequent interruptions. You will have better information to plan for repairs and replacements.

Having a printer maintenance schedule as advised by the manufacturer, using your printer sensibly, using the correct consumables, having a secure setup and a clear support process will give you the best results. Identify which printers are key to your daily operations, note how they are used and plan to have them checked based on their volume. Having a planned schedule is usually easier to manage than waiting for your printer to cause issues.

title: laptop buying guide for small businesses
seoTitle: laptop buying guide for small businesses
metaDescription: Choose business laptops with the right performance, security, durability, connectivity, warranty and lifecycle cost for your small business.
excerpt: Choose business laptops with the right performance, security, durability, connectivity, warranty and lifecycle cost for your small business.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: A laptop is an essential piece of kit for any small business. With the ability to interact with your customers, manage accounts, create documents, attend meetings, run business software and store important information. If you get the wrong laptop you may cause yourself issues with slow applications, short battery life, little connectivity, expensive repairs and devices that aren’t able to support updates.

Small businesses often operate on a budget so you may be tempted to get the cheapest option. However, you may find the downtime, replacement, and support costs could outweigh the initial savings made. Whereas on the other hand you may be spending unnecessarily on high performance options for all members of staff. If most of your roles are using basic functions like email, spreadsheets and web based systems you don’t need to be spending unnecessarily.

When purchasing a laptop for your small business start by considering what each member of your team will be doing. Administrative staff will likely be using email, office software, web based tools, video calling and accounting software. Sales staff may want something light weight with good battery life and connectivity on the go. Whereas designers, engineers, developers and video editors may want something with a higher performing processor, increased memory and dedicated graphics.

Don’t just go for the same spec. Group your roles into a couple of categories. For example, standard office, mobile and specialist. This will make it easier to purchase the correct laptops for everyone. Check the system requirements for any essential business software and look at what hardware your software providers recommend.

Consider how your business may change in the future. You may want to use some new cloud services, handle larger data sets and higher performance software. Ensure your choice provides you with a bit of extra performance to cater for the expected usage over the time between replacements. Don’t get extra that you won’t realistically use.

content.heading: CPU
paragraphs: The CPU will impact how fast your applications will perform, how well you can multitask and how well it will perform when running high performance applications. Most mainstream CPUs will be fine for general office use. However, there are many different types and models and will affect the performance. Look at the exact model, generation, cores and independent reviews.

For general document creation, web based applications and video calling a modern mainstream CPU will be fine. However, if you have developers, analysts and users of specialist software you may want to consider getting a higher performance option. If you have a heavy workload such as compiling, virtual machines, large spreadsheets or media you want to consider this in more detail.

Laptops will also suffer from overheating and power management. Two laptops with the same CPU may perform differently when running long workloads due to the design, cooling and power limitations. Look at reviews for how they will perform when running longer workloads.

content.heading: RAM & Storage
paragraphs: This will affect how many applications and web pages you can have open without slowing down. If you have a basic office role you may be fine with a lower spec. However, it can be useful to get 16GB for most business users that will be multitasking. For specialist roles 32GB or more may be needed.

Ensure your laptop has upgradable RAM. Some slim laptops will have the RAM soldered onto the motherboard. If you are going to use the laptop for a few years it will be better to get enough RAM from the start. If you have a lot of RAM you won’t have to replace it as early.

Try to get an SSD to ensure quick boot up and app opening times. The size will depend on how much you need to store locally. 512GB would be a sensible option for most staff. However, if you have users that will be using lots of media or large data sets you may need more. Don’t rely on the laptop storage to store your important information. Always use approved cloud storage and managed back up solutions. Ensure you can recover your data.

content.heading: Security
paragraphs: As your business laptops may contain customer information, financial information, internal documents and company systems you should consider security. Look at what security features are available for the OS, firmware, secure boot, encryption and biometrics.

Ensure your chosen devices can be updated with OS and firmware updates for the expected lifespan. Ensure your security software, identity and device management platforms can be used with your chosen models. If you have a team you may want to get devices that can be centrally managed. This can help with applying policies, setting up, updating and reacting to lost devices.

Ensure you have standard processes in place for user accounts, multi factor authentication, locking screens, approved software and data storage. Your staff should know what to do if the device is lost. Both the hardware and how its set up will impact the security.

content.heading: Build Quality, Keyboard & Portability
paragraphs: Ensure the laptop is comfortable to use daily and has a good build quality. If your staff are travelling between customer sites a lighter 13/14inch laptop may be better. However, if they are mostly using it from a desk a larger screen may be better. Also consider what the total weight is including the charger and any essential accessories.

Look at the build quality of the hinges, keyboard, touchpad and body. If your staff are typing lots having a well spaced keyboard and backlit keyboard may be beneficial. Ensure the webcam, microphone and speakers are good for regular online meetings. If possible try a sample device.

Many business laptops will have good build quality features such as durable bodies, servicing and longer support periods. However, this will depend on the model family. Look at independent reviews for build quality and what the warranty covers.

content.heading: Ports, Connectivity & External Displays
paragraphs: Small businesses often use their laptops with printers, scanners, projectors, monitors, storage and meeting room equipment. Ensure you know what accessories your staff will be using and that the laptop has the correct ports. Many devices will still use USB-A so it can still be useful. If the USB-C port can be used for data transfer, charging and display then it will be useful. Some roles may need HDMI, Ethernet and memory card slots.

Not all USB-C ports will provide display output or high watt charging. Check the manufacturers technical specifications. If your staff are using docking stations ensure they are compatible with your laptop and how many external displays (and resolution) you will need.

Look at what wireless capabilities the laptop has. Ensure it can connect to your business network using the correct Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. If your staff are travelling you may want to ensure they have a reliable mobile hotspot or a model with mobile connectivity.

content.heading: Battery Life & Charging
paragraphs: If your staff are using the laptop away from their desk, attending meetings around the site or travelling then battery life will be an important factor. The battery life quoted by the manufacturer will be based on specific scenarios and may not give you the full day of video calling and multitasking. Look at independent reviews for the correct workload.

Look at how big the charger is, how quickly it charges and if it can be charged via USB-C. If you have a few models that can be charged with the same charger it will make it easier to have spares. However, ensure the power requirements are met. Decide how your staff will report if the battery is deteriorating and when they will need replacing.

As the battery ages it will affect how well it performs. If it is constantly connected to power it may have different requirements than if it is being used regularly on the go. Follow the manufacturers guidelines for charging and storage. Don’t fall for any battery myths.

content.heading: Warranty, Support & Replacement
paragraphs: If your laptop breaks it can cause some disruption and unexpected costs. Look at how long the warranty lasts, what is covered, where it can be serviced, how quickly it can be repaired, what accidental damage cover is available and if replacement parts are available. Ensure you know if it can be serviced on site and if there is priority support. This may be an extra cost.

Having a few models can make it easier to support your team. Having a few approved models may mean it’s easier to have spare chargers, repairs and standard images. However, don’t push specialist staff into using the wrong hardware.
Having an asset register will help with planning replacements. This will include the model, serial number, who it is allocated to, purchase date, end of warranty date and any repair history.

content.heading: Total Cost of Ownership
paragraphs: When purchasing a laptop you need to consider the total cost of ownership. This includes accessories, licences, security, management, extended warranties, repairs, time to set up and eventual replacement. A cheaper laptop may become slow and unreliable quickly making it more expensive overall. Consider how long you expect to use the device for. Consider the downtime costs and if you need a spare for key roles. Compare the models with the same amount of RAM, storage, screen and warranty. Don’t be fooled by promotional pricing when the spec isn’t the same.

Creating a simple spreadsheet to log the price, key specs, warranty, support options and estimated lifetime cost of each option will help you make a clear decision. This can also help with explaining your decision to the business owners or finance team.

content.heading: Set Up
paragraphs: When purchasing your laptops ensure they are set up. Install any approved OS updates, set up security, add to management tools, install any required applications and ensure the back up and recovery works. Provide your staff with a standard set up guide. This should include passwords, multi factor authentication, updates, data storage and support contacts.

Don’t use one admin account. Each user should have their own account and permissions should be based on their role. Keep track of what devices have been allocated. Ensure you have a secure process in place for returning devices.
Having a standard set up will help to reduce any differences in set up and make it easier to support. This will ensure your laptop is ready to use.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: The best laptop for your small business will be one that matches the workload of the employee, has the correct performance and security and can be supported throughout its useful life. Consider the CPU, RAM, SSD, screen, battery, ports, build quality, warranty and total cost of ownership. Using roles will help to ensure you don’t get under powered devices and are not overspending.

Test a sample model, ensure software is compatible and check the support options. Printerworld can be a great place to start looking at your requirements for laptops and printers however ensure you are making your decision based on the exact models, spec and support options you have available.

title: why choose professional laptop and printer repair services?
seoTitle: why choose professional laptop and printer repair services?
metaDescription: Explore the benefits of professional laptop and printer repair, including accurate diagnosis, safer repairs, suitable parts, data protection and service accountability.
excerpt: Explore the benefits of professional laptop and printer repair, including accurate diagnosis, safer repairs, suitable parts, data protection and service accountability.

content.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: There can be a temptation to search for solutions online or attempt to repair the issue yourself when your laptop/printer has an issue. Whilst there are some simple issues you can safely resolve as a user, hardware, electrical and more complex software issues will require the correct tools and knowledge. Attempting to incorrectly repair an issue could result in damage to a component, an impact on warranty and risk to important data.

Professional laptop/printer repair services will aim to identify the issue and suggest the correct resolution. A good technician will want to gather information and complete tests, they will then explain the issue and discuss repair options. This article will outline why using a professional repair service can be beneficial and what to look for. 1. Accurate Diagnosis

Many issues with devices can have multiple potential causes. With laptops, you may experience shutdowns due to overheating, battery/charger issues, memory issues and OS issues. You may experience poor print quality with your printer due to an issue with consumables, printhead, incorrect settings and worn parts.

Without completing tests repairing may cause unnecessary costs. A professional repair service will complete a thorough diagnosis to identify the correct cause. The technician will want to investigate connections, component health, software settings and recreate the issue.

Ask the service what the diagnosis fee covers. Will it be reduced if you agree to the repair? It’s a good idea to ask for a clear explanation so you can understand exactly what is causing the issue. If there are multiple components that can cause similar issues, it’s important to have a good diagnosis.

content.heading: 2. Less Risk Of Damage
paragraphs: Laptops and printers can be quite fragile with small components, delicate connections and sensitive components. Laptops can be difficult to open with clips, ribbon cables, sticky-back components and specific screws depending on the model. Printers can have many moving parts including gears, rollers, sensors and hot components.

If you don’t have the right tools or experience, you may damage connections, strip screws, damage cables and fit components incorrectly. Repairs involving electrical and batteries should be handled carefully. Never attempt to repair a swollen Li-Ion battery, faulty power adapter or smell of burning.

Professional technicians will handle components correctly. Ask to see if they have any experience with the specific model and if the repair will be suitable for your device. Don’t begin any repairs until you fully understand what will be done and any important risks involved.

content.heading: 3. Correct Parts Used
paragraphs: The reliability of your repair will depend on the parts and how they are installed. Laptops will require specific parts such as batteries, keyboards, screens, fans and storage to match your exact model or hardware revision. Printers will require specific consumables and parts to match the manufacturer.

A professional service will be able to identify the correct part number. They will also be able to explain if the part is an original, approved or compatible part. These can vary in price, availability and warranty. Don’t assume all compatible parts will work the same.

Ask for details of the part and warranty. Sometimes the cheapest part may not be the best option for important devices. The service should clearly explain any compromises. Avoid any claims of high quality or original parts.

content.heading: 4. Data Protection
paragraphs: Your laptop may contain personal photos, business documents, customer details, bookmarked web pages and access to online accounts. It’s important to take reasonable steps to keep your data private. If you can still access your laptop, ensure you back up any important documents. If the device doesn’t power on, let them know if your data is important. Ask them to discuss options to recover your data before doing anything that could cause data loss.

Only give them access to what they need. If possible, create a temporary account with limited privileges. Log out of any sensitive services. If it’s a business laptop, follow your organisations data policy.

Ask how they will handle data on the device. Will they need to access files? Will they need to reset the device? No repair service should guarantee your data will be safe, especially if the storage is failing. Being clear before beginning repairs will help avoid any confusion.

content.heading: 5. Time Saving
paragraphs: Having an faulty device can cause disruption to your studies, business and communications. You may waste hours trying different unproven solutions. A technician with experience of the category of device will be able to identify common failure points efficiently and suggest a realistic solution.

In a business environment it’s important to consider the time of your staff. A faulty printer can cause delays to invoicing or dispatch documents. A faulty laptop can prevent an employee from accessing key systems. The service may be able to advise if it makes more sense to repair, temporarily replace or plan an upgrade.

Ask how long the repair will take. Will it depend on parts being available? A responsible service will be able to give you an approximate time frame. If you need something urgently, discuss what their priority will be and if there are any extra charges.

content.heading: 6. Cost Estimate
paragraphs: A professional service should be clear with their costs. Ask for a cost estimate. Ensure it clearly states the diagnosis charge, labour charge, parts charge, tax and any drop off/pick up charges. Ask what will happen if they identify another issue once they have opened the device. They should ask for your approval before making any significant changes to the cost.

A written repair sheet will help you understand what has been done. It will include the model, issue, condition, approved repairs and parts replaced. Once repaired ask for a summary of what has been done.

Ask if there is a warranty on the repair. What is covered and how long for? There may be different warranties for labour and parts. Keep your invoice and repair details in case the issue comes up again.

content.heading: 7. Improve Print Quality With A Professional Service
paragraphs: Printers can have a variety of issues. You may experience streaks, faded text, colour issues, connectivity issues, constant error messages and print queue issues. This can be caused by mechanical, electrical, consumables or software issues.

A technician can check for maintenance messages, paper path, rollers, printhead/imaging unit (depending on the model). They may also check drivers, network settings and print settings. This is useful if your printer is working mechanically but unable to receive print jobs from your office network.

A professional service can also help you decide if it’s worth repairing. If the device is old, parts are not readily available or a high cost part is needed it may be more cost effective to replace. A good recommendation will include comparing the cost of the repair to the expected life span of the device and cost of a suitable replacement.

content.heading: 8. Fix Hardware And Software Issues
paragraphs: Laptops can require a variety of repairs. This can include replacing the battery, repairing the keyboard/screen, fan and cooling system, upgrading storage, testing memory, OS troubleshooting and diagnosing charging port issues. The correct approach will depend on the model and issues.

Software issues can also be an issue. Your laptop may have corrupt drivers, update failures, malware, damaged user profiles or storage issues. The technician should explain if there is a risk of losing applications or personal files. Don’t assume re-installing or resetting will be harmless if your data hasn’t been backed up.

Once repaired, test everything that was having an issue. Charging, keyboard, screen, Wi-Fi, audio, ports and performance. For printers run some suitable test prints to ensure it can print from the correct computer/network.

content.heading: 9. Choosing A Reliable Service
paragraphs: Choose a service that supports your specific brand/model. They should be able to explain their diagnosis process. Ask for clear cost estimates. Ask if they have experienced technicians, where they source parts from, if there is a warranty on the repair and how long it will take. Reviews can be useful, look for detailed trends.

Avoid any unrealistic guarantees, unclear pricing and pressure to approve expensive work. Ask for clear explanations of the diagnosis. If applicable ask for the parts to be returned. If it’s a business device, confirm they can follow your organisations security/access policies.

Whilst it’s handy to have a local service, ensure they are transparent. Printerworld can be a good option to enquire about laptop/printer support. Confirm they currently offer the service, what models they can support, what the charges are and what the warranty covers.

content.heading: 10. Preparing Your Device
paragraphs: Write down the model and serial number. Note the issue and when it started. Take pictures of any visible damage. Back up important files. Remove any memory cards/USBs (unless they are part of the issue). If it’s a business device, get approval from your IT/security team.

Don’t leave any unnecessary passwords, payment details or confidential documents. Ask for a repair reference and receipt to show they have accepted your device. Ask if they will contact you before replacing any parts or re-installing.
When collecting your device, check the condition. Ensure they have fixed the issue and ask for a summary of the service. If possible test everything that was having an issue.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Using a professional laptop/printer service will give you an accurate diagnosis, less risk of damage, correct parts, clear costs and documented repair. This can be very beneficial if there is an internal hardware, electrical, important data or recurring issue.

Choose a service that can explain what they will do, respect your privacy, ask for your approval for any extra charges and have clear warranty details. Whilst simple checks can be useful for small issues, if there are ongoing or safety issues it is best to use a qualified service. This will ensure the device works reliably and help you make an informed decision.

title: Meet Printerworld: Your One-Stop Shop for Printers, Laptops and Repairs
seoTitle: Meet Printerworld: Your One-Stop Shop for Printers, Laptops and Repairs
