Check your manufacturers documentation to see what they are storing, how long they are storing them for and if they have any automatic delete or secure erase options.

If your printer is being moved, reallocated or decommissioned treat the internal memory as business data. Follow the secure wipe/memory clean process. If your printer contains sensitive information consider using an approved support team. Simply switching off or doing a factory reset may not be enough.

content.heading: 9. Secure Device/Output
paragraphs: Ensure your printer is located in an area that isn’t easily accessible to visitors. If it is in a public reception area don’t print sensitive information. Ensure covers are closed during maintenance.

Ensure your employees have a routine for picking up their jobs. They should pick them up quickly, ensuring they have printed all pages and removing any errors. Ensure you have a secure shredder or approved confidential bin for any documents you no longer need. Leaving paper around your printer can cause issues even if your network settings are great.

content.heading: 10. Printer Security Checklist
paragraphs: Ensure your printer has a record. This should include model, serial number, location, network connection, admin owner, firmware version, support status, last reviewed and updated by. If you have a new printer ensure you follow a checklist. This should include changing passwords, network, services, firmware, access and secure disposal.

Periodically check your printer and after any major changes to your network/staff. If your printer has unexpected settings, is sending unexpected emails or acting strangely disconnect from your network if possible. Contact your IT administrator. Ensure you have any logs/error messages.

content.heading: 11. Decommission
paragraphs: If your printer is no longer receiving security updates it can pose an ongoing risk to your business. If it is connected to your business network or dealing with confidential information contact the manufacturer to ensure it is still supported. If it no longer meets your security requirements consider replacing it. Balance this with if it can be fixed, availability and if your business actually needs it.

If you are looking to sell/recycle your printer ensure you wipe your data as per manufacturers recommendations. Remove any saved network information and contacts. Reset your settings. Ensure any removable memory is securely handled. Follow your organisations retention policy and local e-waste requirements.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: To secure your office printer you should look at securing your networked device and output. Change default passwords, update firmware, limit network access and disable any unnecessary services. Use secure print for sensitive documents, limit scan locations and secure any stored data. By using a simple checklist and regularly reviewing your printers you will make printer security a standard part of your office IT.

title: 10 Laptop Accessories That Boost Productivity
seoTitle: 10 Laptop Accessories That Boost Productivity
metaDescription: Discover ten practical laptop accessories that can improve comfort, organisation, connectivity and productivity at home, school or work.
excerpt: Discover ten practical laptop accessories that can improve comfort, organisation, connectivity and productivity at home, school or work.

content.heading: Introduction: Make Your Laptop Work Better for You
paragraphs: Laptops are made to be portable however they can have some issues when used for long periods of time each day. This can cause issues such as a small screen, uncomfortable keyboard and limited ports. However adding the correct accessories can make your laptop more comfortable and useful without changing the whole laptop.

To start with you don’t need to get everything. Think about what you use the most and what is causing you a problem. A student may want a mouse and sleeve whereas someone who works remotely may want a monitor, headset and stand. Here are 10 great options:

content.heading: 1. Laptop Stand
paragraphs: Laptop stands will elevate your screen and can help you have a more ergonomic position. This can help you avoid hunching over the desk. There are different types you can choose from, fixed, adjustable, folding or portable. Make sure you pick a stand that can support your laptop size and weight.

Ensure that the stand doesn’t block any of the ventilation on your laptop. If you’re raising your screen then an external keyboard and mouse will help to get your hands into a comfortable position. This is not a complete solution to ergonomics but can help your workstation.

content.heading: 2. External Keyboard
paragraphs: An external keyboard can be a great addition if you’re using a stand or larger monitor. This can give you a more familiar keyboard, special navigation keys or just a more comfortable typing experience. Wired keyboards are easy to set up whereas wireless keyboards can help to reduce cable clutter.

When choosing think about the keyboard layout, spacing, connectivity and compatibility with your Operating System. If you often use multiple languages then ensure the keyboard will have the correct layout and connectivity. Your keyboard should be comfortable to type on.

content.heading: 3. Wireless/Ergonomic Mouse
paragraphs: A mouse can help you select text, edit spreadsheets, design software and manage multiple windows quicker than using just the touchpad. Wireless mice can be very flexible. Wired mice won’t need to be charged. Ergonomic can be more comfortable for some but this depends on personal preference.
Ensure that your mouse fits your hand size and workspace. Check if it’s Bluetooth or USB and your laptop has the correct connectivity. Ensure it’s close to your keyboard.

content.heading: 4. External Monitor
paragraphs: An external monitor can help with extra screen space when working on documents, coding, spreadsheets, research and video calls. This can help you avoid having to constantly switch between windows. Choose the correct size and resolution for your desk. Ensure your laptop can support the connection and display.

Think about the panel type, brightness, adjustability and port availability. Ensure you have it at a comfortable distance and reduce glare from windows or lights. If you’re using your laptops screen as a secondary screen then a stand can help you with positioning.

content.heading: 5. USB-C Hub/Docking Station
paragraphs: Modern laptops can often have limited ports. A USB-C hub will help with extra connections for USB, memory cards, displays and sometimes wired network connections. A docking station can give you a more permanent single cable setup with multiple displays.

It’s important to ensure it’s compatible. Not all USB-C ports will support video, charging or the same data speeds. Ensure your laptop meets the hub requirements and check the display, charging and number of ports supported. Choose a reliable adaptor and ensure it has the right power rating. If you’re using an external monitor then ensure it can charge.

content.heading: 6. Headset/External Microphone
paragraphs: Having good audio can really help during online lessons, customer calls and team meetings. A headset can help you avoid background noise and echo from the speakers. Some have a boom mike which can help bring the microphone close to your mouth. Wireless mouses can help you stay flexible whereas wired can be simpler and don’t need charging.

Ensure it’s comfortable, good quality microphone, correct connectivity and compatible with your meeting software. Try your headset out prior to an important call. Ensure your microphone is in the correct position. If you’re often presenting or recording then a dedicated USB microphone can give you more consistent audio. Ensure it’s in the right place and you’re in a quiet area.

content.heading: 7. Laptop Sleeve/Backpack
paragraphs: A padded sleeve or compartment will help protect your laptop from scratches and light bumps. Ensure it’s the right size for your laptop and won’t put pressure on the screen. A backpack with a dedicated compartment can help you store your charger, notebook and accessories.

This will depend on how it’s made, how well it fits and how you use it. A sleeve won’t fully protect from dropping or squashing. Ensure any liquids are in their own sealed compartment. Don’t place anything heavy on top. Ensure your laptop is powered down or in the correct power mode before travelling.

content.heading: 8. External Storage/Backup Drive
paragraphs: An external SSD or hard drive can help give you extra space for large projects, images, videos and backing up. SSD’s are small and generally faster. HDD’s can give you more space for less per GB. Choose based on size, speed, portability and connectivity.

Try to back up regularly rather than just when you remember. Ensure you have at least one backup away from your laptop. If you’re doing confidential work then look at using an encrypted drive. Follow your organisations storage policies. Whilst this can be useful it shouldn’t be your only copy of important information.

content.heading: 9. Laptop Cooling Pad
paragraphs: A cooling pad will help circulate air with fans. This can be useful for some models to help keep airflow when working hard. This can be useful for gaming or long periods of use. However it will depend on your laptops intake and how well the cooling pad lines up. This won’t help if your fan isn’t working, or there is a blockage in the heatsink or dust build up.
Ensure it’s stable and doesn’t block any of the laptops vents. Check if it’s noisy and the correct power connectivity. If your laptop is overheating during normal use then find out why.

content.heading: 10. Privacy Filter/External Webcam
paragraphs: A privacy filter can help reduce the viewing angle of your laptop screen. This can make it harder for people next to you to see what you’re doing in public areas. Ensure you know the exact measurements of your screen and how it attaches. Some can reduce the brightness and effect touchscreen. Ensure it’s compatible.

An external webcam can help with positioning and image quality if you’re often using video calls. Ensure it has the correct resolution, field-of-view, low light, microphone options and how it attaches. Ensure it’s at eye level and follows your privacy policies at work.

content.heading: How to Choose Accessories Without Spending Too Much
paragraphs: Pick the accessories that will help you with a recurring issue. If you’re often typing for long periods then a keyboard may be more important than nice lighting. If you’re often travelling then a sleeve and small charger would be more useful than a big docking station. Ensure it’s compatible, has a warranty, good build quality and return policy.

Don’t plug too many power hungry devices into a poor quality hub. Use approved chargers and cables from the manufacturer with the correct power rating. Keeping your desk tidy, internet reliable and good backup habits can help increase your productivity.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: The best laptop accessories will help you avoid any issues during your daily use. Adding a stand, keyboard, mouse and monitor can help your desk setup. A hub, headset and storage can help with certain workflows. A sleeve will help protect whilst travelling. A cooling pad or privacy filter can help in certain scenarios. Start with the biggest issue you have daily and ensure it’s compatible.

title: 7 Features to Look for in a Home Printer
seoTitle: 7 Features to Look for in a Home Printer
metaDescription: Compare seven important home-printer features, from printing technology and connectivity to duplexing, scanning and running costs.
excerpt: Compare seven important home-printer features, from printing technology and connectivity to duplexing, scanning and running costs.

content.heading: Introduction: Choose for the Printing You Actually Do
paragraphs: A home printer can be used to print school work, forms, documents, travel documents, labelling and photos. Depending on what you need to print regularly you may require a printer with basic functions and compact size. If you have a couple of students or remote workers in your household then you may want something that prints quickly, has scanning capabilities and low running costs.

Have an idea of how many pages you're likely to print per month and if you require colour printing. Think about the following 7 points to ensure you get the best printer for your needs. To avoid getting a printer that is cheap to buy but costly to use, think about the following factors:
Printing Technologies

content.heading: Inkjet Printers
paragraphs: These use liquid ink. Often these are great for printing documents with various colours and photos. Inkjet printers come in a variety of styles including ink cartridge printers and refillable tank printers. Ink cartridge printers will often be cheaper to buy however, if you’re printing lots of colour, the refillable tank option may be a good choice. Inkjet printers require some proper maintenance if they are going to be left for a long period of time.

content.heading: Laser Printers
paragraphs: These use toner powder. These are often great for printing text based documents. Monochrome laser printers are a great choice for printing school work, invoices and forms. However, colour laser printers may be more costly to buy. Think about what you’ll be printing and how many pages you expect to print per month.

content.heading: Total Cost of Ownership
paragraphs: Although you may be tempted by the initial price of the printer, make sure that you know how much the ink/toner will cost to replace. How many pages do they claim to print? The page yield will be tested by the manufacturers using standard conditions, however this may not be the same as your documents (especially if you’re including photos, large images or lots of colour).

Think about the cost of the paper, maintenance, printhead cleaning, spare parts and whether there is a warranty. Work out how much you’re likely to pay over 2-3 years. If you’re only printing a few pages per month then a simple, low cost printer may be enough. However if you’re printing regularly then an economical printer may be a better choice.

content.heading: Wireless & Mobile Print
paragraphs: Print over Wi-Fi so multiple devices can be connected to the printer within your household. Some printers can be printed to from mobile devices using apps from the manufacturer. Ethernet can be handy if the printer will be close to your router.

Make sure the printer is compatible with your computers, phones and operating systems. Think about how easy it is to set up and if you need an account with the cloud. Although wireless printing is handy you should ensure that your network is secure. Try to use a secure network at home and change the default admin login if possible.

content.heading: Automatic Duplex Printing
paragraphs: This means the printer will automatically print onto both sides of the paper. This can save you using as much paper for reports, notes and longer documents. If you regularly print study or work documents this can be very useful.

Check if the printer can duplex the paper sizes you require. Some printers only allow manual duplex printing whilst others allow automatic duplex. Not all documents will need duplex printing so make sure the printer can easily be changed in the driver.

content.heading: Scan & Copy
paragraphs: Some printers have a copy and scan function. This can be handy when you need to scan signed forms, copy school documents or keep digital copies. A flatbed scanner is a good option if you’re only printing single pages, books and fragile documents. Some printers have an automatic document feeder which can be more convenient.

If you regularly scan double sided documents then make sure the printer can duplex with the automatic document feeder. Are there any file types you can scan to? If you’re not going to be using the advanced scanning functions then make sure you’re not paying for them. However if you regularly handle documents then think carefully.

content.heading: Paper Sizes, Speed & Volume
paragraphs: Make sure the printer can handle the paper sizes, weights and types. Basic home printers will often only be able to print standard A4 paper. Some printers can handle envelopes, labelling and photo paper. If you’re printing large volumes of documents then make sure the paper tray can hold plenty of paper. A small paper tray will need to be filled more regularly.

The printer speeds will have been tested under certain conditions. This may not reflect how long it takes to print your first page, colour images or complicated documents. Make sure you look at how fast it can print and the recommended monthly volume. If you’re only going to be printing occasionally then the printer may struggle if a couple of people are sending large print jobs throughout the day.

content.heading: Easy to Maintain, Support & Warranty
paragraphs: The printer should be easy to set up, fill and maintain. Make sure the ink/toner cartridges/bottles can be easily replaced. Is the control panel easy to understand? Are there official drivers for your devices? What is the manufacturers warranty?

Think about how the printer reacts when running low on supplies. Does it give helpful error messages? Can you find genuine or compatible supplies from reliable retailers in your area? A printer that is difficult to maintain can be frustrating even if the print quality is good.

content.heading: Additional Factors
paragraphs: How much space will the printer take up? Consider the tray sizes and how much space it takes up when the trays are open. If the printer can fit on a shelf when closed it may take up a lot of space when you put paper in or collect the printouts. If you’re in a small apartment or shared working space then noise could be an issue. Look at independent reviews.

If the printer connects to your network then make sure it’s connected securely via Wi-Fi. Ensure the firmware is up to date. Make sure you can easily collect your personal documents. If the printer has internal storage or can scan to the cloud then make sure you understand how it deals with your data.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: A good home printer will have the correct printing technology, low running costs, easy to connect, good paper handling and reliable support. Whilst automatic duplex and scanning can be a useful addition, they aren’t essential for everyone. Work out how much you’re likely to print, think about the cost of the supplies and make sure it’s compatible. The right printer will allow you to complete your regular tasks easily without costing you too much.

title: Intel vs AMD Laptops: Which Processor Is Right for You?
seoTitle: Intel vs AMD Laptops: Which Processor Is Right for You?
metaDescription: Understand Intel and AMD laptop processors by performance, battery life, graphics, price and workload before choosing your next laptop.
excerpt: Understand Intel and AMD laptop processors by performance, battery life, graphics, price and workload before choosing your next laptop.

content.heading: Introduction: Look Beyond the Brand Name
paragraphs: Both Intel and AMD produce processors for a variety of laptops.
Whilst each brand provides various families their products will vary in performance. It is not possible to know which laptop you're getting from just the brand.

The performance of the laptop can depend on what generation of processor it is, exact model, TDP, cooling and the rest of the laptop specs. Laptops with processors from the same company can vary greatly between models due to the cooling, ram and power management. Check the whole package of the laptop and look for unbiased reviews.

content.heading: 1. Know the model and generation of the processor.
paragraphs: Both brands have naming and model numbers to identify different families of processors. These can sometimes change over time so don't always go off the assumption that a higher numbered model means it's newer/faster. Check the exact model and generation on the official spec sheet.

Look out for how many cores the processor has, threads if applicable, clock speeds, cache, TDP and the type of memory it supports. Whilst this gives some useful info, it won't give you the real world performance. Some processors will be designed for thin and light laptops meaning they'll be more energy efficient, whilst others may have a bigger cooling system.

content.heading: 2. Performance for general use such as studying/office.
paragraphs: Most current Intel and AMD processors will be more than sufficient for web browsing, email, video calls, office tools and general studying. The keyboard, screen, battery, RAM, SSD and build of the laptop may be more of an issue than the small difference in CPU benchmarks.

Ensure you have enough RAM for how many apps you'll be running. An SSD will help your system boot up quicker and open files quickly. If your work is mostly document based and online learning, you won't usually need to pay extra for a high-end processor.

content.heading: 3. Performance for development and creative uses.
paragraphs: Development can sometimes involve using code editors, local servers, virtual machines, containers and compiling. Creative applications can use either the CPU, integrated graphics or a dedicated GPU. Whilst having more cores can help with parallel processing, some applications may rely on single thread performance.

Check what your exact requirements are. If you're doing big software builds, 3D or video editing you might want a higher performing processor, extra RAM and dedicated graphics. However, some thin laptops may throttle the processor if they can't effectively cool during extended periods of work.

content.heading: 4. Integrated graphics and gaming.
paragraphs: Many Intel and AMD processors have integrated graphics which can perform well for general use, video playback and some light gaming. The performance can vary greatly depending on the generation of the processor, graphics and memory bandwidth. If you're wanting to play demanding modern games and creative applications that require high GPU usage, it is generally better to get a laptop with a dedicated graphics processor.

Check what the real world benchmarks are for the exact laptop. The cooling, ram and TDP can impact how well the graphics perform. If gaming is important to you, you should check the GPU, refresh rate, cooling and charging requirements.

content.heading: 5. Battery life.
paragraphs: The battery will be affected by many factors such as the screen size and brightness, battery size, wireless use, background apps and power settings from the manufacturer. Both Intel and AMD have energy efficient processors for portable systems, as well as higher performance ones.

Look for unbiased battery tests. A larger battery may give you longer battery life despite the processor being similar. A high resolution or high refresh rate screen may cause the battery to drain quicker. If portability is important, look at the whole laptop and see what the tested battery life is.

content.heading: 6. Heat and fan noise.
paragraphs: A high performing processor will require good cooling. A small laptop may get quite hot and have noisy fans during extended periods of work. A larger laptop may perform better as there will be more space for heat pipes, fans and airflow.

Look for reviews that test real world performance and temperatures. Check where the vents are and ensure they won't be blocked on your desk. Neither Intel or AMD guarantee a cooler laptop. It can depend on the chip and how the laptop is designed.

content.heading: 7. Price.
paragraphs: Look for laptops that are similar in price. If the processor looks like it would perform better in benchmarks but the screen, RAM, storage and build aren't great then it may not be the best value for money. However, if the laptop is lighter, quieter and cheaper despite having a slightly weaker CPU it may be a good choice.

Check if the laptop has a good warranty, service and upgrade options. Some laptops have soldered RAM/storage so it may not be easy to upgrade. Ensure you check these details before purchasing especially if you expect your software requirements to increase.

content.heading: 8. Who are you buying for?
paragraphs: Students and general office users will usually want a modern entry/mid range processor with enough RAM and SSD. Developers will want to check how many cores, RAM and support for their tools. Video editors and designers should check the benchmarks for their applications and if they need a dedicated GPU. Gamers should check the whole graphics setup and cooling.

If you're buying for a business fleet it may be easier to have a standardised set of options. Ensure the laptop is compatible with your OS, docking, security features and warranty service. Check the CPU performance.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Both Intel and AMD have great processors for laptops. Depending on what exact processor you're getting, cooling, graphics, RAM, battery, screen and price it may be better to go for one over the other. Decide what your main applications will be and look for reliable reviews on the exact models. Go for a balanced system. For many general users the overall quality of the laptop will be more important than the processor badge..

title: Printer Not Connecting to Wi-Fi? A Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Guide
seoTitle: Printer Not Connecting to Wi-Fi? A Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Guide
metaDescription: Fix common wireless printer connection problems with practical checks for Wi-Fi, router settings, drivers, network bands and printer setup.
excerpt: Fix common wireless printer connection problems with practical checks for Wi-Fi, router settings, drivers, network bands and printer setup.

content.heading: Introduction: Find Where the Connection Is Failing
paragraphs: A wireless printer not connecting can be a nuisance both in the office or at home. This can cause the printer to be offline, not appear in device list or not connect during initial setup. This can be due to network settings on the printer, the router, password changes, poor signal strength or the print queue on your computer.

To troubleshoot, start by confirming the printer is connected to the network, then confirm the computer/phone is connected to the same network. Finally confirm that the printer can be discovered. Try to avoid doing a factory reset unless you have noted any important network settings.

content.heading: 1. Confirm the printer supports your Wi-Fi network
paragraphs: Check the printer specifications to see what wireless standards and frequencies it supports. Some older printers only support 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Newer routers may have both 2.4 and 5GHz networks but may combine them into one network name. Some set up processes will require either your phone or computer to be connected to a specific frequency.
If your printer doesn’t support the correct frequency or security settings on your network, it may not connect properly. Check the printer manual and router documentation.

content.heading: 2. Power cycle the printer and router
paragraphs: Sometimes a simple power cycle will fix any temporary networking issues. Turn the printer off using the power button. Wait a few seconds then turn it back on. Power cycle the router using the guidelines provided by your internet provider or router manufacturer. Once the network is up try reconnecting your printer.

Try to avoid constantly pulling devices from the network as they may be receiving firmware updates or maintenance. If you can’t connect to the internet on other devices, it could be a problem with the router or your internet.

content.heading: 3. Confirm the correct Wi-Fi name and password
paragraphs: If the password on your router has changed, your printer may still be trying to connect using the old password. Navigate to the wireless settings on your printer and select the correct network name. Enter the new password carefully. Passwords are case sensitive and can often be confusing if there are similar letters.
If your router uses separate network names for each frequency, choose one that your printer supports. Don’t use a guest network as this could mean your computer can’t find your printer.

content.heading: 4. Ensure the printer is close to the router
paragraphs: Poor signal strength can cause problems with the setup process, causing the printer to drop out occasionally. Place your printer close to the router. Avoid placing it in a sealed cabinet or behind thick walls. Large metal objects can cause issues with the wireless signal.

If your printer connects when close to the router, you may want to improve the position of your printer, or invest in a mesh Wi-Fi system. Some environments may benefit from a Wi-Fi extender. However, ensure it is set up correctly. Don’t place your printer somewhere that will block airflow or access to paper trays.

content.heading: 5. Ensure your computer is on the same network as your printer
paragraphs: Most local wireless printers will require your computer or phone to be able to communicate with the printer. Ensure your computer is not on a guest network, mobile hotspot or separate VLAN. In an office environment, networking policies may be in place to stop devices communicating.

If your printer has a network status page, print this out and check the status. Add your printer using the official app or OS settings. Don’t manually enter an IP address unless you have confirmed it is the correct IP for your printer and know if it will change.

content.heading: 6. Check for errors on your printer
paragraphs: Check your printer for errors such as ‘Failed to connect’, ‘Authentication Error’ or ‘Wireless Off’. Some printers will have a wireless set up wizard or network status report. Check the instructions for your exact model. Note down any error codes.
If your printer says it is connected but your computer shows it is offline, it could just be an issue with your printer settings. Check the print queue, driver and device.

content.heading: 7. Clear print queue and reboot
paragraphs: If your printer has a stuck print job it can appear to be unresponsive. Open the print queue on your computer and cancel any obvious stuck print jobs. Reboot your computer if needed. Print a small test page. Ensure you are printing to the correct printer.

If you can print using multiple devices but just not your computer, focus on your computer settings. If you can’t print from any devices, check your printer is connected to the network and sharing the network.

content.heading: 8. Update or reinstall official driver
paragraphs: If your driver is out of date or damaged, your computer may not be able to communicate with your printer properly. Go to the official support page for your printer manufacturer. Search for your exact model and download the driver for your operating system. Follow the instructions to install the driver. Remove any old duplicates.

Don’t use driver packages from unknown websites. If your printer is working on your mobile device but not your computer, reinstalling the official driver can be very helpful. Reboot your computer if prompted during the set up.

content.heading: 9. Check your router settings
paragraphs: Some routers have options such as client isolation, access control, MAC filtering or guest networks. These can stop your computer from communicating with your printer. In a managed office environment, your network may be segmented.

Don’t disable your security settings on your router or put your printer onto the public internet. If you are unsure what is stopping your printer from being found locally, contact your network administrator or internet provider. It is more important to keep your printer secure.

content.heading: 10. Reconnect using the wireless wizard
paragraphs: If none of the above have worked, reconnect your printer using the wireless wizard. Before doing a factory reset, note down any information you may need such as the network name, password and static settings. Follow the manufacturers instructions for reconnecting your printer. Don’t just do a general factory reset.
Once reconnected, check your printer has a network address. Print a test page. Add your printer to all required computers/mobile devices using the official set up.

content.heading: When to contact technical support.
paragraphs: If your printer isn’t finding any compatible networks, keeps dropping out when close to the router, there is an error relating to the wireless hardware or isn’t connecting even after correct set up, contact your manufacturer, network admin or a qualified technician. Provide them with your printer model, router type, error message and what you have tried so far.

If other devices are having issues connecting to Wi-Fi, contact your internet provider or router support. If it is just your printer, it could be an issue with the wireless module, firmware or settings..

title: Why Is My Laptop Battery Draining So Fast? And How to Fix It
seoTitle: Why Is My Laptop Battery Draining So Fast? And How to Fix It
metaDescription: Find common causes of fast laptop battery drain and learn how to improve battery life through settings, apps, screen use and battery care.
excerpt: Find common causes of fast laptop battery drain and learn how to improve battery life through settings, apps, screen use and battery care.

content.heading: Introduction: Understand What Is Using the Power
paragraphs: There could be multiple reasons why the laptop battery isn’t lasting, such as a bright screen, intensive applications and background processes, low wireless signal, peripherals and battery age. The battery life will depend on different factors including the screen size, processor, graphics and battery size.

The first thing to consider is how you are using the laptop. If the laptop is being used for general web browsing it may last a few hours, but if it is being used for more intensive uses such as gaming, video editing or video calls it could drain quicker. This will help you identify if you are wasting power and if there is an issue with the battery getting old or a hardware issue.

content.heading: 1) Reduce the screen brightness
paragraphs: The screen can be one of the biggest power consumers on many laptops. Try to reduce the screen brightness to a comfortable level. If your laptop has an auto brightness feature, try to see if this is working correctly. You can also set your screen to turn off quicker by reducing the timeout. If the laptop has a high refresh rate screen, try to change this to a standard refresh rate for everyday use. Do not have the screen too low that it becomes uncomfortable to read.

content.heading: 2) Disable any background applications
paragraphs: Some background applications may be using too much power, this can be seen by opening task manager on Windows or activity monitor on Mac. Close any applications you don’t need that are using a high amount of resources. Ensure you don’t close any applications you don’t know what they are. Some applications will be using resources due to security software, cloud syncing and OS updates. However if you notice any 3rd party applications are constantly using power whilst you aren’t using them, update them or change their settings.

content.heading: 3) Use power saving mode on the OS
paragraphs: Most laptops will have a power saving option. Changing to an energy saving or balanced option will reduce the background processes and reduce the power the processor is using. The options may vary between different operating systems and manufacturers.

If you are using the laptop for something intensive, change to a higher performance option. If you are just using it for documents, browsing and emails then a balanced option will often be enough. Some laptops will have extra options within their manufacturer’s software. These options can include thermal and power profiles.

content.heading: 4) Minimise battery intensive applications
paragraphs: Using the laptop for video calls, gaming, streaming, graphics and multiple tabs with media in can be intensive. If you are noticing the battery isn’t lasting as long when doing something specific, check to see what the laptop is using more power on. Try to turn off any unnecessary visual effects and close any tabs you aren’t using. If possible, reduce the performance of the applications.

For long meetings, check if using a headset or external monitor is affecting the battery. External monitors can cause the laptop to use more power as they require their own power source. However this can cause the laptop to put more strain on the graphics. Test with the setup you would normally use.

content.heading: 5) Disable Wi-Fi & Bluetooth and peripherals
paragraphs: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth can cause the laptop to use more power. Disable Bluetooth and any USB peripherals which are draining power. If your Wi-Fi signal is weak then the laptop can also use more power.

Try to ensure the laptop is located somewhere with a strong network connection. Avoid having any external drives, hubs or phones connected which aren’t being used. Some peripherals will use power so removing them can help. However this may not be as big of an issue as the screen brightness and performance.

content.heading: 6) Update the OS and drivers
paragraphs: Updating the OS and drivers can improve the power management, sleep and compatibility issues. Update using the OS or the official support software provided by the laptop manufacturer. Reboot and check if this helps.

Avoid installing random driver update software. Only update the BIOS and firmware if it is the correct time to do so for the model. Always ensure you have a stable power source and never interrupt an update.

content.heading: 7) Check the battery condition
paragraphs: Batteries will start to lose their capacity over time. If the laptop used to last 8 hours but now is losing its charge very quickly after many charges, check the battery condition within the OS. If available, check the battery condition using the manufacturer’s diagnostics software. Check what the full charge capacity is and compare it to the original design capacity. This may not be exact.

If the battery condition isn’t great and the battery isn’t lasting as long as it should, it may be worth replacing it with a compatible one. Use an authorised or reputable service provider to ensure you get the correct part number. If the battery is sealed, do not attempt to open it. If the manufacturer states it can be replaced by the user, follow their instructions.

content.heading: 8) Avoid overheating
paragraphs: Overheating can affect the performance of the battery. Ensure the laptop is on a hard surface and the vents are not blocked. Do not place the laptop in direct sunlight. If the laptop is heating up too much when doing light tasks, check the vents are not blocked, there are intensive background processes and if there is an issue with the cooling.

Do not place the laptop in a fridge or use any liquids to cool it down. This can cause condensation due to sudden temperature changes. If the battery is swelling, the case is lifting or there is an odd smell coming from the laptop, stop using and charging the laptop. Get it looked at by a qualified person.

content.heading: 9) Change sleep/hibernate settings
paragraphs: If the laptop is in sleep mode and the battery is draining, this can be due to background processes, network and peripherals. Change the sleep settings within the OS. Choose the correct setting based on how long you will be putting the laptop to sleep for. If you are putting the laptop into storage or taking it out, follow the advice provided by the manufacturer. This will include turning the laptop off and setting the battery to a certain level.

If the laptop is waking up unexpectedly, check the scheduled tasks, peripherals and wake settings. If a device is using a lot of power when it is turned off completely, there may be an issue with the battery, firmware or hardware. This will need to be diagnosed.

content.heading: 10) Turn on battery saver
paragraphs: Battery saver can help reduce background syncing, notifications and more. Turn on battery saver when the battery is at a certain level. Some laptops will have smart brightness, energy suggestions and battery reports for each application.

These features will help increase the battery life by reducing some of the processes. It is important to understand the trade-off. If you need instant notifications and background uploads, adjust the settings. It is better to have a good balance rather than turning everything off.

content.heading: When should I replace my battery?
paragraphs: If you are noticing the battery isn’t lasting as long, the device is shutting down unexpectedly whilst the battery still has power, the battery is not recognised or charging stops at an unusual level, ask for a battery assessment. If the battery is swollen, overheating, leaking, smoking or causing the case to lift, seek urgent service. Never press, poke or squash the battery.

Before seeking service, make sure you have backed up any important files. Note down the model of your laptop, battery issues and charger details. Ask for a compatible battery to be fitted. Ask for the part to be under warranty. If the laptop is old, see if it is worth repairing.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: The battery could be draining quickly due to the screen brightness, intensive applications, background processes, wireless, power settings or just getting old. Check the reports for how you are using the laptop, change the settings sensibly and ensure it isn’t overheating. If the battery condition is poor, get a compatible battery fitted. If the battery is swelling or overheating, stop using the device and get it looked at by a professional. Making small changes can help increase the battery life. However, if the battery is old it won’t be able to be fixed by changing the settings.

title: How to Choose the Right Printer Paper for Documents, Photos and Presentations
seoTitle: How to Choose the Right Printer Paper for Documents, Photos and Presentations
metaDescription: Learn how paper weight, finish, brightness, size and printer compatibility affect results for everyday documents, photographs and presentations.
excerpt: Learn how paper weight, finish, brightness, size and printer compatibility affect results for everyday documents, photographs and presentations.

content.heading: Introduction: Paper Is Part of Print Quality
paragraphs: Selecting a quality printer paper can impact the quality of your finished prints. Choosing the right paper will ensure your print is sharp, coloured, dries quickly and feeds through your printer reliably. You may find different papers are needed depending on whether you are printing an invoice, photograph, brochure or presentation.

Paper can come in many varieties, it will have different weights, thicknesses, finishes, brightness and coatings. Make sure you select the correct paper for your printer and what you are printing. Check your printer’s media options and select a quality paper relevant to your print.

content.heading: 1. Select the Correct Paper for your Printer
paragraphs: Inkjet printers use liquid ink to print your documents. Inkjet papers are designed to absorb and retain the ink effectively. While regular copy paper can be used for text, photographs and coloured graphics often look better on a coated inkjet paper to help control bleeding and increase detail.

Laser printers use toner powder which is melted onto the paper. The paper needs to withstand the heat from the printer. Not all inkjet coated papers are suitable for laser printers. Check the packaging for what printers are suitable and follow the manufacturer guidelines for what media they recommend.

content.heading: 2. Know the Weight
paragraphs: Paper is often measured in grammes per square meter (gsm). Standard office paper will often be 70-80gsm. Thicker papers can be used for reports, covers and presentations. The higher the number the thicker the paper will be. However the thickness can vary depending on how it is made.

Don’t just go for a heavier paper. Ensure you are within your printer’s weight range and check your trays. Very thick media may need to be inserted into the manual feed or rear feed. Inserting media that your printer does not support may cause jams, poor fusing on a laser printer or uneven ink absorption on an inkjet printer.

content.heading: 3. Plain Paper for Regular Print
paragraphs: Multipurpose plain paper is a good option for regular printing. This can include emails, invoices, forms, notes and reports. It is usually an affordable option and readily available. As most of these documents will contain text, it is usually more important to have a good quality paper that will feed through your printer reliably.

If you have charts/coloured graphics, consider upgrading to a quality office paper. This can help your text to look cleaner and colours to be more consistent. Try printing a small amount first to ensure you are happy with the paper. If you will be using this for an important regular project, try printing a small amount first.

content.heading: 4. Photo Paper for Photographs
paragraphs: Photo paper is designed to give you more detail, colour and contrast in your prints. There are many finishes available including glossy, semi-gloss, satin and matte. Glossy papers can give you vibrant colours. Matte papers can limit glare and may work better for framed images or designs.

Ensure you’re using photo paper that will work with your printer. Within your print settings select the correct paper type. This will affect how the ink is applied. If you do not select the right option, you may experience smudging, dull colours or too much ink. Allow your prints to dry/cure as advised by the manufacturer before stacking or framing.

content.heading: 5. Presentation Papers
paragraphs: Often presentation papers will look more premium. Using a heavier matte or satin paper can give your reports, handouts and proposals a more premium look whilst still being easy to read in an office environment. Glossy papers may be useful for marketing images, however they can cause glare from overhead lights making it harder to read text.

Think about how you’ll be using your document. If it is going to be handed out at a meeting it should be durable. If it is going to be printed for reference within the office, you may not need a premium paper. Choose a finish that will help you to read the document.

content.heading: 6. Check the Size
paragraphs: A4 is widely used in many countries for office documents. However you may be printing a different size for letters, labels, envelopes or photos. Ensure the paper in your tray matches the size you’ve chosen for your document. If it does not match, you may experience cropped prints, scaling issues or feeding problems.

When printing envelopes or labels, ensure you are using the correct feed path. Follow the diagrams to insert the media correctly. Not all printers will take all envelopes/labels. Check the maximum size of media, printable area and tray instructions.

content.heading: 7. Brightness and Opacity
paragraphs: Brightness relates to how much light is reflected off the paper. Whiteness relates to the shade of the paper. A bright paper can give your black text more definition. However brightness and whiteness are not the same. Different manufacturers may measure their paper differently. Try comparing samples in the light you’ll be viewing your documents in.

When printing double sided, you want to ensure the paper is not too thin so text/images do not show through. If you need to print double sided, choose a suitable weight and opacity. Try printing a sample of the paper with a typical document.

content.heading: 8. Store Correctly
paragraphs: Paper can absorb moisture from the air. This can cause the paper to curl, stick together or feed inconsistently. Very dry paper can cause more static. Store your paper flat in its packaging in a clean, dry environment. Avoid direct sunlight, heaters and spillages.

Only insert the amount of paper your printer recommends. Don’t leave any spare paper in the tray for long periods of time in humid/dusty environments. If the paper has curled, is damp or damaged, replace it.

content.heading: 9. Select the Correct Settings
paragraphs: Ensure you have the correct paper type selected in your print settings. This could include plain paper, matte photo paper, glossy photo paper, labels or envelopes. Depending on your device, this can affect how the ink is applied, how fast it prints, how the fuser works etc.

If your print is too dark, smudged or not fusing well, ensure you have the correct paper and settings selected. Ensure you have the right size, source tray and quality. Take note of the settings that work well so you can recreate them for regular printing projects.

content.heading: 10. Try a Sample
paragraphs: Print a sample of your presentation, brochure or photos. This will ensure your colours look good, everything is lined up, easy to read, has dried and feeds through. Printing a sample will help you avoid wasting resources.

If you’re printing something important for business/event, try a few different papers and finishes in realistic lighting. Keep the sample with the packaging information so you can order the same again. It is important to have consistency.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Choosing the correct printer paper will depend on your printer, what you’re printing and what you’re using it for. Plain paper is great for regular printing, photo paper can improve your images and heavier papers for presentations can give your reports a more premium look. Ensure you have the correct weight, finish, size, opacity and compatible paper. Select the correct settings in your driver. The best way to ensure you have the correct paper is to print a sample..

title: Laptop Battery Replacement: Signs It Is Time and What to Expect
seoTitle: Laptop Battery Replacement: Signs It Is Time and What to Expect
metaDescription: Recognise common signs of laptop battery wear, understand replacement options and prepare safely for a battery service.
excerpt: Recognise common signs of laptop battery wear, understand replacement options and prepare safely for a battery service.

content.heading: Introduction: Batteries Wear Gradually
paragraphs: Laptop batteries are consumable items that will degrade over time. The capacity to hold a charge will reduce over time, resulting in more frequent charging. This may be a natural part of the aging process. However, if there are issues such as random shutdowns, charging issues or puffing you should pay extra attention.

Replacing an old battery can help give mobility back to your laptop. Deciding to replace your battery should be based on many factors including battery health, age of device, cost of repair and safety. The below guide will help you know what to look out for, how to check battery health and what to expect.

content.heading: 1. Reduced Runtime
paragraphs: One of the most obvious signs that a battery is old is experiencing a significant drop in runtime. If your laptop used to last for several hours doing the same tasks but now is running out of charge very quickly it could be due to a loss of capacity. Try comparing similar tasks and brightness settings. Video calls, gaming and intensive applications will drain the battery quicker than document editing and browsing.

However, a sudden drop in runtime could be due to software issues. Always check your operating systems battery report to make sure it is not a software issue. If there isn’t an improvement after checking software settings then check battery health.

content.heading: 2. Random Shutdowns
paragraphs: An old battery can cause your laptop to randomly shut down after displaying how much charge is left. The percentage can be an approximate and may not be accurate if the battery has become uncalibrated or the cells are failing. If your laptop is regularly shutting down then ensure you frequently save your work and back up any important documents.

Random shutdowns could also be due to overheating, a faulty charger or another hardware issue. If the issue is only happening when running on battery power then it may help a technician identify if it is a battery issue.

content.heading: 3. Low Capacity
paragraphs: Many laptops will show battery health through the operating system or manufacturer diagnostics. This report may show you the original design capacity and the current full charge capacity. If there is a significant difference then it means the battery is holding less energy than it used to.

Battery health reports are approximate. However, if there are regular warnings during diagnostics or the manufacturer shows battery health, then you may need to look into replacing with a suitable battery. Don’t always go solely off the percentage.

content.heading: 4. Long/Unreliable Charging
paragraphs: If your battery is taking an excessive amount of time to charge, refusing to charge or not charging to the expected level then it may be due to the battery being old or faulty. However, the charging can be affected by many things such as temperature, charger wattage, power management settings and battery protection. Some laptops intentionally do not charge fully to keep the battery healthy in the long term.

Always use the original or manufacturer approved charger and cable. Check that there is no visible damage to the charging port. Never use any tools or liquids in the charging port. If you are experiencing intermittent charging or the port is getting hot then do not use the device.

content.heading: 5. Puffing
paragraphs: If your Lithium-Ion battery is puffing then it shouldn’t just be replaced for convenience. You may notice that your touchpad is raised, keyboard is raised, gaps in the casing, the base is bulging or the laptop is no longer flat. It may also feel very hot or have an odd smell.

If you think your battery is puffing then stop using and charging. Never push down the casing, pierce the battery, bend or remove it unless you are trained and following the manufacturers emergency guidelines. Ensure it is kept away from flammable items and get it looked at by a qualified service.

content.heading: 6. Correct Battery Part Number
paragraphs: Each laptop has a specific battery. Even if the laptops are the same brand they may have different battery shapes, connections, capacity and firmware. To find out what battery you need look up using the exact model and battery part number. A good place to start would be the manufacturers support page.

Don’t just go off a picture in the marketplace or one that looks similar. Check that it is compatible, correct voltage, connection type, capacity and the reputation of the supplier. Using a low quality or incorrect battery can cause charging, performance and safety issues.

content.heading: 7. Original / Compatible / 3rd Party
paragraphs: The original manufacturer batteries may be the easiest way to ensure compatibility. However, a compatible 3rd party battery can be cheaper. Quality and reliability can vary between suppliers so check who you are buying from. Check they have a good reputation, warranty, safety certification (where applicable) and returns policy.

Don’t always go for the cheapest option. Ask your repairer if it is an original or 3rd party part and what warranty is provided. If the laptop is for critical business use then you may want to prioritise support and reliability.

content.heading: 8. What Will Happen During Repair?
paragraphs: The technician will identify your laptop model and check the battery for any damage. Depending on the design of the laptop the battery may be easily removed via an external latch or may be fitted internally. If it is internal then the technician will use the correct tools and method to avoid causing any damage to cables, clips or the battery.

They will replace with a compatible part, secure the connections and carry out any checks to ensure charging and system is working properly. Ask if they will check the charging port and power adapter. If the battery is puffing then they should follow safe handling and disposal practices.

content.heading: 9. Back Up Data
paragraphs: Before handing over your laptop back up any important documents. If possible write down the model and serial details and what issues you’re experiencing. Also what charger you are using and any battery warnings. Follow any guidelines the service provider has in relation to passwords. Usually you won’t need to wipe the storage however it is a good idea to prepare.
If your laptop is under warranty then contact the manufacturer or authorised service. Check the terms and if it isn’t covered get a written quote.

content.heading: 10. Responsible Disposal
paragraphs: Laptop batteries should never be disposed of in general waste. They contain materials that should be disposed of correctly. Ask your service provider if they will take the old battery back. Alternatively use an authorised battery or e-waste drop off point.

Never expose damaged/puffed batteries to heat, pressure or metal. Don’t store loose batteries with keys/coins that could cause a short. Follow your local guidelines and don’t try to open the battery pack.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: You may need to replace your laptop battery if you’re experiencing a significant drop in runtime, random shutdowns, poor battery health from diagnostics or unreliable charging. If the battery is puffing or getting unusually hot then you should take immediate precautions and get it looked at by a qualified service. Check the exact battery part number, compare your options and back up your data. A suitable battery can prolong the lifespan of your laptop which would otherwise be suitable for you..

title: How Long Do Printers Last? Lifespan by Type and How to Extend It
seoTitle: How Long Do Printers Last? Lifespan by Type and How to Extend It
metaDescription: Explore typical printer lifespan factors, differences between inkjet and laser models, warning signs and maintenance habits that support longer use.
excerpt: Explore typical printer lifespan factors, differences between inkjet and laser models, warning signs and maintenance habits that support longer use.

content.heading: Printer Lifespan Depends on Use and Care
paragraphs: Each printer will have a variety of factors affecting how long it can be used for. The amount of printing done will vary significantly between a home printer printing just a few pages a month and an office printer printing hundreds of pages a day. Factors such as the design of the printer, build quality, maintenance, environment and availability of consumables and servicing will effect how long a printer can be used.

Rather than aiming for a certain number of years, it can be helpful to look at the overall condition of the printer and if it is still providing good value for money. A printer may be faulty or not provide good value due to lack of consumables, no longer being supported for security issues or repair costs being too high. It is important to understand why a printer would last a certain amount of time to ensure you are looking after it properly and know when it is time to replace it.

content.heading: 1. Inkjet and Laser Printers
paragraphs: Inkjet printers use liquid ink and have a printhead with tiny nozzles. Inkjet printers can suffer from ink drying and blockages in the nozzles if left unused for long periods. A clean cycle can sometimes resolve this issue but will use extra ink. Other parts like feed rollers and maintenance pads will also have a limited lifespan.

Laser printers use toner powder. They have various parts such as imaging drums, transfer units, fusers and feed rollers. Some parts can be replaced by the user but some need servicing. Laser printers may be able to cope with high volumes of text printing but will still depend on the duty cycle, environment and maintenance.

content.heading: 2. Duty Cycle and Volume
paragraphs: The manufacturers may give a duty cycle and suggested print volume per month. A duty cycle is usually the maximum amount that can be printed in a month and a suggested print volume will give a more realistic view.

Ensure you use a printer appropriate to your printing needs. If you consistently use a low volume home printer to print a higher volume intended for a departmental office, it can cause extra wear and may cause more issues. If you are printing a higher volume consider using a printer designed for this.

content.heading: 3. Environment
paragraphs: Ensure that your printer is kept in a clean environment. Ensure you are using a steady flat surface and allow for air flow and paper trays. Avoid placing your printer in areas that may cause issues. Avoid placing your printer where there may be spillages, cooking oil, dust from a workshop or constant knocks.

Keep your paper in a dry area and protect it until you are ready to use. If the paper is damp or curled it can cause issues with feeding. Keeping a clean environment will not guarantee no issues but will reduce unnecessary wear on parts.

content.heading: 4. Correct Paper and Consumables
paragraphs: Ensure you are using the correct size, weight and type of paper. Ensure your paper trays are not overloaded and the guides are adjusted so that your paper sits firmly in place without any bending. Remove any damaged paper and don’t mix media types unless your printer allows.

Ensure you are using the correct ink/toner for your exact model. Using incorrect or low quality ink can cause leaks, recognition issues, inconsistent prints and damage. Keep your unused cartridges in their original packaging. Don’t overstock as you may not be able to use all of them. This also affects how practical an older printer can be.

content.heading: 5. Keep Clean
paragraphs: Wipe the outside of your printer with a soft lint free cloth. Follow the instructions in your manual to clean any rollers, glass and other parts that can be cleaned by the user. Follow the cleaning instructions if your printer has specific instructions. Don’t spray any liquid inside your printer. Don’t use any domestic solvents inside your printer.

Only clean your inkjet printhead if you have an issue with the nozzles (as indicated by a nozzle check). If you clean frequently you’ll waste ink and will fill up your maintenance pad. Laser printers have sensitive imaging parts and may have hot parts. Don’t touch the drum or open up sealed units. If there is a lot of dust inside your printer you may want to get it professionally cleaned.

content.heading: 6. Don’t Overload
paragraphs: Too many paper jams can cause wear on your feed rollers. Ensure you are using the correct paper for your printer, ensure it is loaded correctly and don’t force the paper in. If you have a paper jam follow the instructions from the manufacturer to remove the paper in the correct direction. Don’t pull too hard and don’t use sharp objects.

If you are having regular paper jams in the same area have it looked at. There may be an issue with your rollers, sensors or paper guides. If you force the paper through it can cause a small issue to become a larger and more expensive fix.

content.heading: 7. Firmware and Drivers
paragraphs: Keeping your software updated can help keep your printer compatible with your current computers and network. Check the manufacturers official website for drivers and firmware updates for your exact model. Follow the instructions for installing these. Don’t use non-official driver tools.

If your printer is connected to a network it is important to ensure it is still supported for security. Change any default admin details if possible and ensure it is on a secure network. Check what support the manufacturer provide. If your printer is still printing but isn’t receiving important security updates it may be time to replace it in a business environment.

content.heading: 8. Signs of Ageing
paragraphs: Your printer may be reaching the end of it’s life if it is causing lots of feeding issues, making noise, giving inconsistent prints, lots of service alerts and repair costs are increasing. Just because it is having one issue doesn’t mean you need to replace it but if there are regular issues it is worth noting.

Keep a log of any repairs, maintenance parts and consumable costs. If you are having regular issues with the same printer compare the total cost of repairs to a new printer with similar capacity and better support. Consider how much downtime you are getting and how much time staff are spending trying to fix issues.

content.heading: 9. Worth Repairing
paragraphs: It can be worth repairing your printer if it is generally a good printer, there is only one issue and parts are available at a reasonable cost. Replacing a roller, cartridge or other part may give you a reliable printer again. Get a written quote and ask if any other parts are likely to need replacing soon.

Check that consumables are still available for your older printer. If it is cheap to repair but you can’t get consumables for it then it won’t be useful for long. Compare the repair quote to the price and running costs of a suitable replacement.

content.heading: 10. Simple Maintenance
paragraphs: Simple maintenance can include checking your paper, wiping the outside of your printer, checking your prints, dealing with error messages and following the manufacturers maintenance schedule. Keep your printer manual and part numbers to hand. In a shared office set someone to report regular issues and order consumables.

Don’t unnecessarily clean your printer or open it up if the manufacturer do not recommend it. Ensure you are carrying out the correct maintenance for your model. It is more useful to take care when using your printer and repair issues when they arise.

content.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: How long your printer lasts will depend on the workload, design, environment, consumables, maintenance and support. Inkjet and laser printers will have different wear but keeping the correct paper, using the correct consumables and taking care with your printer will help. If you are having regular issues and repair costs are increasing it may be time to replace it. With good maintenance your printer can last a long time but no printer will last forever..

title: The Complete IT Equipment Checklist for a New Office Setup
seoTitle: The Complete IT Equipment Checklist for a New Office Setup
metaDescription: Plan a new office technology setup with a practical checklist for computers, networking, printers, security, accessories and ongoing support.
excerpt: Plan a new office technology setup with a practical checklist for computers, networking, printers, security, accessories and ongoing support.

content.heading: Introduction: Plan the Work Before Buying Equipment
paragraphs: Setting up your IT infrastructure can be a complicated process. You need to make sure you are investing in the right products and that your equipment can support the tasks your organisation needs to carry out. It should also keep your business data secure, and allow for easy management as your team grows. Choosing the wrong equipment will result in incompatible accessories, poor network coverage, unnecessary subscriptions, and having to replace equipment.

Start by thinking about what roles you are employing, what software they will be using, how many people you will have working within your office, and what type of data they will handle. Think about what equipment you will need to get straight away and what you will need going forwards. The list below are some common areas you will encounter. The list should be tailored to your business based on the size, industry and security requirements.

content.heading: Computers & Laptops
paragraphs: Ensure you choose your computers based on the roles your employees will be carrying out. General office roles may require reliable laptops/desktops with enough memory, SSD storage, the correct processors and comfortable screens. If your employees have specific roles such as design, engineering, software development or data analysis then you might need higher performance computers with more powerful processors, extra memory and dedicated graphics.

Where possible try to keep your configuration standard. This will make it easier for deployment, support, spares and replacements. Ensure you know what warranty and support you have for your operating system, what service you can get and if your computers can be upgraded. Decide whether your employees will need laptops, desktops or a mixture.

content.heading: Monitors, Keyboards & Mice
paragraphs: If your employees will benefit from extra screens, get them a monitor. Ensure it has the correct resolution, size, adjustable screens and compatibility with your chosen computers. If your employees are sitting at a desk you might want to get external keyboards and mice to make things more comfortable.

If appropriate, get monitor arms or stands. Ensure your desks can support them. Where possible try to keep the connections standard so your employees can easily plug into their equipment. Have a small amount of approved cables and peripherals to hand for replacements.

content.heading: Printers, Scanners & Multifunction
paragraphs: Decide whether you need individual printers, network printers or multifunction. Think about how many pages you expect to print per month, do you need colour printing, what size paper you will need and how many people will be sharing the printers. A small team might just need one reliable multifunction printer, whereas a larger office might need separate printers for different departments.

Look at the total cost of ownership. This should include ink/toner, paper, maintenance parts, service and expected downtime. Ensure your printer can print double sided, has scanning capabilities, network capabilities and security. Shared printers should be placed where your employees can easily collect documents without showing any confidential outputs.

content.heading: Network Router, Switches & Wi-Fi
paragraphs: Having a reliable network is essential. Having a business router/firewall and Wi-Fi access points that are suitable for your organisation size, expected devices and internet service. Larger areas might need several access points or managed network equipment.

Where possible ensure devices that will benefit from a stable connection have an Ethernet cable. This could be desktops, network storage or a shared printer. Ensure you have enough switches to cover your required ports. Ensure your cables are labelled. If you have guests you will need separate Wi-Fi. If your office is complex or has more than one floor, have a qualified network professional look into coverage and security.

content.heading: Internet & Backup Connection
paragraphs: Ensure you select an internet package suitable for your number of employees and what they will be using. If there are lots of video calls, cloud backups and large file transfers make sure you have a good upload speed. Look at service level agreements, time frames for installation, support and data limits.

If your business cannot afford to lose internet, consider having a backup connection. This could be a second provider or mobile broadband. Ensure you can easily switch to your backup connection. Ensure you have the details for your provider and who to escalate to, in a secure place.

content.heading: Security & Access
paragraphs: Before your employees start using business systems, plan your security. Use an approved operating system, endpoint protection, automatic updates, strong authentication and multi factor authentication on important accounts. Ensure you have individual accounts for your employees. Give them the minimum access they need to carry out their tasks.

Ensure your router and Wi-Fi are secure. Change default passwords and limit access to admin. Ensure you have a process in place to add/remove employees. This should include turning off their accounts and getting back your company devices. If you have regulated or sensitive information, seek advice on what you need to comply with.

content.heading: Backups & Storage
paragraphs: Decide where you are storing your business files. This might include approved cloud storage, network attached storage or both. Decide what data needs to be backed up regularly, who can access it and how long it needs to be kept.

Ensure you have a backup strategy in place. This should include ensuring your data is safe from being accidentally deleted, hardware failure and ransomware. Ensure you test your backups regularly. Don’t assume just because you have synchronisation this is a full backup. There might be unwanted changes that get synchronised. Ensure you have a process in place for recovering your data, and who is responsible for checking your backups.

content.heading: Power & Cables
paragraphs: Ensure you have the right sockets for your computers, monitors, network and printers. Use reputable surge protectors where appropriate. Choose products that are rated for what you will be connecting. Don’t overload your sockets.

If you have critical equipment consider using an UPS. This should be sized to your expected load and time. This gives you time to safely shut down your equipment. This should be maintained and tested. Ensure your power and network cables are organised and labelled. Don’t have them running across walkways.

content.heading: Collaboration & Communication
paragraphs: Your employees might need collaboration tools. This could include email, calendars, messaging, video calls, document collaboration and project management. Ensure you have tools that are suitable for your business. Check the licencing, how many users can use them, storage, administration and exporting data.

Ensure you have a standard process for setting up accounts. Provide some basic guidance for your users. Don’t buy duplicate subscriptions until you know what is included in your current subscriptions. Know who is responsible for renewals, payments and permissions.

content.heading: Software, Licencing & Device Management
paragraphs: Ensure you know what operating systems and applications each role will need. Ensure you have proper licencing, they are assigned to the correct people and supported. If you have a larger organisation and higher risk, consider using central device management. This can make it easier to configure, update and apply security.

Keep a device register. This should include what type of device, model, serial number, who it is assigned to, purchase date, warranty and software. Keep your recovery keys and admin in approved secure systems.

content.heading: Office Equipment & Meeting Rooms
paragraphs: Depending on your office you might want devices such as laptop docks, webcams, headsets, speakers, presentation screens, adaptors, charging stations and document shredders. Meeting rooms might need a screen, video call camera, microphone and reliable Wi-Fi/Ethernet.

Ensure you test your equipment in the room. Ensure your cables can reach, audio is clear and your video calling is compatible with your hardware. Provide simple guidance so your employees can get started without any help.

content.heading: Support, Maintenance & Replacements
paragraphs: Decide who your employees should contact if they have an issue. Small offices might have an external IT support team, whereas larger organisations might have internal IT. Ensure you have a process to report, prioritise and track issues. Keep your vendor contacts, warranty details and device details in a place where authorised people can access them.

Ensure you have a schedule to check your software updates, backups, printer supplies, network equipment and check the condition of your hardware. Plan your budget for replacements. Ensure old computers, drives and printers are disposed of securely.

content.heading: Conclusion – Secure & Scalable Office
paragraphs: Having a full IT setup for your office includes the right computers, monitors, printers, network, security, backups, power and support. By starting with your employee processes and business needs, keeping your equipment standard where possible and adding maintenance into your budget you will have an office that can run reliably from day one. Keeping a register, clear access processes and testing your backups will make your office easier to scale in the future..

title: How to Protect Your Laptop from Viruses and Malware: A Practical Guide
seoTitle: How to Protect Your Laptop from Viruses and Malware: A Practical Guide
metaDescription: Protect your laptop from viruses, ransomware and other malware with practical habits for updates, downloads, passwords, backups and safe browsing.
excerpt: Protect your laptop from viruses, ransomware and other malware with practical habits for updates, downloads, passwords, backups and safe browsing.

content.heading: Everyday Habits Are Your First Line of Defence
paragraphs: Laptops hold important information such as personal files, work files, pictures, passwords and online accounts. This can be vulnerable to malware. It can cause problems like slowing down your computer, displaying adverts, stealing your credentials, or encrypting files for a ransom. There are many ways that your laptop can become infected.

You cannot guarantee that a single security tool will stop all attacks. By using supported software, secure account settings, careful web browsing, regular backups and being aware of any suspicious activity you can increase the security of your laptop. The steps below are good steps to take from home users, students and small businesses.

content.heading: 1. Keep your Operating System updated
paragraphs: Many updates for your operating system will include security patches. Make sure that you turn on automatic updates where possible. Install any important security updates as soon as possible, and restart your laptop where required so that the updates can be completed properly.

Ensure that your OS is still supported by the developer. If it isn’t getting security updates it will be more difficult to keep secure. If you cannot run a supported version consider upgrading your OS or replacing the device instead of relying on Anti-Virus.

content.heading: 2. Use trusted security software
paragraphs: Use the built-in security tools of a supported OS or use a reputable security tool from a known provider. Turn on real-time protection and automatic updates. Run a scan if you notice any unusual activity or if a security alert suggests you should.

Avoid using multiple real-time anti-virus tools unless they are explicitly supported by their providers. This can cause conflicts, slow your laptop and cause confusing alerts. Do not trust pop-ups stating that your computer has a virus and asking you to call an unknown number.

content.heading: 3. Download from trusted sources
paragraphs: Download any applications from the official developers site, a recognised app store or an organisation approved software portal. Be very careful with the spelling of the sites. Some sites will mimic popular applications and include installers with unwanted/malware.
